rows.summary: Six resting limits per 15m structure flip (stop at anchor, target at 0.41), clustered by flip. The gate compared GB levels (0.705/0.7475/0.79) with the concept's own control set (0.5/0.618/0.786). Control-adjusted difference −0.002R, powered NULL (46k fills pooled, 20.9k in the gated arm).

Trade: first 15m close beyond 0.41 after a flip, plus threshold_fits displacement (N=4, r=1.5, d=0.65), then a limit back at 0.41 toward 0.7475 with stop at the extreme (0.82R). Beat the matched random entry by +0.051R. Halves: H1 +0.011, H2 +0.087 (H2-heavy). Net avg R is still −0.012. p=0.03, so this is only a candidate and unlikely to survive Holm/BH.

Trade: blind limit at 0.7475 of a 15m valid-flip range (the anchor→high range extends until the fill), stop at the anchor, target 0.41 (1.34R), 24h expiry or next opposite flip. Result −0.008R versus the matched control, powered NULL (MDE 0.042).

Gate on the GB 0.7475 book: three or more arrays (level + unmitigated 15m/1h FVG, order block, 50% of the extreme wick) overlapping the 0.705-0.79 zone vs fewer. Fired on 594 of 6970 fills (8.5%). Result −0.068R, wrong sign, and UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.155).

Trader T reading: a 1h fractal sweep, then a 5m close through the relative fractal from before the sweep. Limit at the latest 5m FVG of the shift, stop at the sweep extreme, 2R, cancelled if the target trades first. Result +0.006R, powered NULL.

$niper reading: prior-day high/low taken, then a 15m MSS with an FVG within 6h. Limit at the FVG, stop at the sweep extreme, target the opposing prior-day extreme (median 4.6R), missed if the target trades first. Result −0.009R, UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.196).

Gate on Trader T's book with no cancel rule: fills before the 2R price traded (86.6%) vs fills after price had already run to the target. Difference +0.0005R, essentially zero. UNDERPOWERED because the cancelled arm is small (546; MDE 0.235).

Gate on the $niper prior-day-sweep/MSS/FVG book: limit in the premium/discount half of the MSS leg (sweep extreme to leg extreme) vs the wrong half (53% pass). Result −0.117R, wrong sign, UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.38, book n=793).
Same $niper book, but the range is the current trading day's running high/low: limit in the correct half vs not (75% pass). Result −0.159R, wrong sign, UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.40, effective n 202).

Tested a daily PO3 anchored at the NY midnight open, with 15m bars. The trigger is the first close back through the open after a manipulation that also closes through the pre-extreme swing. Only breakers overlapping the open were traded: limit at the breaker edge, stop beyond the manipulation extreme, target open+2SD, exit at 17:00 NY. Result: +0.097R vs control, CI straddles 0, n=304, so UNDERPOWERED. This is the second run: the first (clock hold) gave exposure_bars 848 vs 765, so it was re-run once with hold_basis=bars as trap 7 directs. Both runs are noted in the result.

The rule's only operative step is footprint/DOM confirmation (tape speed, buy/sell aggression) at the ICT level. The data is M1 OHLC spot XAU_USD with no volume, no trade-side classification and no order book. The guest also gives no threshold for any of it.

Tested option A, the 50% mark of an oversized gap (5m FVGs at least 1 ATR(20)), against the near-edge entry he warns against, on the same gaps. Stop at the far edge, 2R target, 50min hold, clustered by gap. Control-adjusted +0.035R, CI contains 0, powered (MDE 0.059), so NULL.

Tested as a target rule on the phase-3 locked 1h CISD entry book: target = near edge of the nearest unmitigated opposite 1h FVG (ladder step 1), stop at the protected swing, 10h hold. Against a control with matched stop and target distances: +0.017R, CI contains 0, powered, so NULL. Unfilled FVGs do not act as magnets.

Structural Silver Bullet: a 1h close through a breaker after a sweep. Stop at the reversal extreme, target the 5-day original consolidation, 48h hold. Gate: the Silver Bullet forms below 50% of the dealing range. Result +0.107R, CI excludes 0 in the claimed direction, but only 497 events in the complement arm (MDE 0.150), so UNDERPOWERED.
The conflicting time-window definition, applied as a gate on the same structural breaker book: the breaker bar is the 10:00-11:00 NY hour. Result -0.007R, n=167 gated, so UNDERPOWERED.

Pooled the five spoken 1h STRAT reversals (2-2, 1-2-2, 3-2-2, 2-1-2, 3-1-2), entered on the M1 trigger through the prior bar's extreme with day-candle timeframe continuity. Target = opposite extreme of the bar before P, stop = other side of P, 10h hold. Result -0.003R vs control, powered (MDE 0.023), so NULL. Continuations were not tested because the guest states no magnitude for them.

15m extreme wick: at least 60% of the range and a sweep of the prior 20-bar extreme. Wait for the wick's 50% to rebalance within 4h, then a stop-entry beyond the wick candle; stop at the wick extreme, 2R, 150min hold. Result -0.074R, CI straddles 0, MDE 0.120, so UNDERPOWERED, leaning negative.

On phase-3 1h CISD order blocks, compared a limit at the wick extreme (start of the wick-to-body band) with a limit at the 50% mean threshold on the same blocks. Stop beyond the block, 2R, 10h hold, clustered by block. Result +0.008R, powered (MDE 0.072), so NULL: the band is no more sensitive than the mean threshold.

Baseline was bare 15m CISD (2R, 150 min hold). The gate kept only reversals whose run swept a still-untaken 15m 2/2 swing formed in the prior 20 bars (22% of events). It added nothing, and the test was powered (MDE 0.040).

Same 15m CISD baseline, gated on the run sweeping the previous day's high or low while it was still untaken. Only 1.4% of events pass. The point estimate is near zero and the MDE is 0.112, just above the 0.10 threshold.

15m breaker continuation: swing low L1, then swing high H, then L1 swept before any close above H, then a close above H within 20 bars. Traded only with the prior day's direction. Entry at the close through H, stop on the swept low, 2R. No better than a matched random entry (powered, MDE 0.037).

Same breakers, entered on a retest instead: the first bar within 10 bars that trades into the body zone and closes beyond its far side, with the stop on that far side and a 2R target. Zero difference from a matched random entry (powered, MDE 0.065).

Baseline was 5m CISD in the direction of the prior 1H candle (2R, 50 min hold). Gate: the decision falls in the first 15 minutes of the current 1H candle (time share 0.25). No effect (powered, MDE 0.031).
Speed reading on 15m CISD with max_wait 10. Gate: the close-through lands 3 or fewer bars after the extreme (a fast V), against 4 or more (consolidation). No effect (powered, MDE 0.031).

Inside the 4H C2 model (one-sided C2 on the forex grid, plus an aligned 15m CISD inside C2), C3 entries with an intracandle CISD were compared with all other C3/C4 model entries, clustered by C2. They are not better (powered, MDE 0.073). Scored on control-adjusted R, not raw win rate.

4H C2 on the forex grid. Entry at the C3 open, stop on the latest 15m CISD protected swing inside C2, which had to sit beyond C2's EQ (xMFd_kfmIqI selection test). 2R target, 240 trading-minute hold (hold_basis bars). Not better than a matched random entry (powered, MDE 0.053).

'Invalidation very close to the open' variant: daily C2, 1H protected swing within 0.25 of the C2 range from the close, held one session. Only 32 events in 10.5 years, because the swing is usually the day's extreme, far from the close. Cannot be decided.

Reading A (a close beyond the CE invalidates the gap). The first CE touch of a 1H FVG closing beyond the CE but inside the gap reaches the far edge within 600 trading minutes 91.2% of the time, against a distance-matched null of 91.0%. The null is not time-of-day matched. Effectively zero, but the MDE of 0.024 is just over the 0.0225 threshold. The A-vs-B dispute is not supported in either direction.

Respect reading: the first CE touch of a 1H FVG closing back on the respecting side reaches the displacement leg's extreme within 600 trading minutes 51.8% of the time, against a null of 52.7%. The null is not time-of-day matched. No continuation edge (powered, MDE 0.021).

Bias-invalidator reading: the first 1H close through the previous day's EQ, against that day's direction, reaches PDL/PDH by the end of the day 49.6% of the time, against a time-of-day-matched null of 49.3% (powered, MDE 0.039). This is the corrected run. The first locked run had a null without time-of-day matching and read EDGE: +0.033 [+0.006, +0.061], p=0.017. Then 28% of events turned out to sit in the 19:00 NY hour (trap 9), so it was re-run once with sample_times(tod_tol_min=30). The notes say this, and both runs are in the ledger.

Expansion-filter reading: 15m CISD trades with the prior 4H candle's direction, gated on the current 4H candle's running extreme having stayed beyond the prior 4H candle's EQ (47% of events pass). Positive but not significant (powered, MDE 0.052).

15m trend: trend = displacement confirmed by the threshold_fits gate. Short/long the next open after an opposing candle closes, stop at that candle's extreme, 2R, 150 min. Returned +0.078R vs control, but this is probably a stop-geometry artefact: it sits almost entirely in the smallest stops (Q1 +0.23R, Q4-Q5 ~0), and a random-direction noise book with the same stop placement also came back EDGE.

Older candle-level definition (NgFIza9qsGQ): an opposing candle in the trend has its near extreme broken, then a limit at the block open, stop at the far extreme, 2R. Marginal EDGE (+0.022R, p=0.03). It leans toward small stops, so the same stop-geometry caveat applies (noted in the result).

Four-point failure-swing block with no sweep (bbWPoajy2MY), retest of the zone candle body. Tested with claim '-' because he says price runs through these. NULL: the retest neither under- nor outperforms. No SMT filter (needs a correlated instrument).

First entry per trend episode among inducement / mitigation-block retest / cheat code (the 15s option was left out). 95% of the book is cheat-code entries, so it inherits the same small-stop concentration (Q1 +0.21R, Q5 -0.04R) and the same stop-geometry artefact caveat.

Canonical box (HFfChGFHD44): an old 2/2 swing is taken with an FVG out and an FVG back in, then a limit on the retest of the highest/lowest body level, stop at the deviation extreme, 2R. NULL (powered, MDE 0.075).
Earlier 'catch them right away' reading (E6bpY4dQvlE): the same setups entered at the close back inside the range. NULL.

After a 15m CISD reversal: opposite FVGs from the prior leg are closed through, then retested as support/resistance. Stop at the protected swing, 2R (stop and target borrowed from the method spec because the concept gives neither). NULL.
Projection as target: 15m CISD entry, stop at the manipulation extreme, target the -2 projection of the leg from the origin swing to the extreme, 12h hold. NULL.

Band as reaction area: on the first touch of -2 (before the extreme is retaken, within 24h) trade the retracement, target -1, stop -4, against a matched control at the same geometry. A well-powered NULL (diff 0.000R).
Gate on the 15m rung-0 CISD book (both directions): shorts closing below the previous-day low (or longs above the previous-day high) vs the rest, claim '-'. NULL: chasing beyond PDH/PDL is not worse.

Same baseline book. Gate: the signal closes at fresh intraday lows (shorts) or highs (longs) relative to the day so far. These trades do worse, -0.038R control-adjusted with both halves negative: EDGE for the concept's claim '-'. Modest p=0.02, so only a candidate pending Holm/BH.

Each fired 15m displacement leg: limit at the discount FVG (capped at the leg's EQ), stop at the leg start, 2R. The order is re-anchored when the next same-direction leg fires, cancelled on an opposite leg or after 24 bars. The book is every fill. NULL.

4H gold/silver SMT, then the lagging (held) asset trades through its level within 20 bars, and gold is traded as a reversal at that close (stop at the extreme, 2R, 40h hold). Result: -0.040R vs matched control, CI [-0.116, +0.039], MDE 0.111 above the 0.10 threshold. Only the two-asset arrangement could be tested; the triad arrangement needs a third market.

Gate test on a 1H gold swing-sweep reversal book (9,483 trades). The gate is an SMT against the named gold-triad member XAU/EUR, built from gold and EURUSD H1, and fires on 27% of the book. Gated arm +0.020R vs complement, CI [-0.051, +0.091], MDE 0.102 just above the 0.10 threshold. XAU/GBP could not be built because the lab has no GBPUSD series.

1H gold/silver SMT reversal book (7,796 trades) decided one bar after the SMT. Gate 'genuine' (62% of trades): the sweeping asset closed back inside its level and the held asset has not caught up. Genuine minus fake = +0.005R, CI [-0.066, +0.074], MDE 0.1002, so power just misses. The visual strength-switch cues are not separately operationalised.

Same 1H gold/silver SMT book. Gate 'stage2' (38% of trades): on the next bar either a PSP (opposite-colour closes) or a candle-2/candle-3 SMT. Two-stage minus one-stage = +0.004R, CI [-0.061, +0.069], powered (MDE 0.093), so NULL: the second stage adds nothing.

Setup: a 1H SMT reversal with a swing formed, and the draw (the prior opposite-side swing) still unmet. Trade the first two-stage PSP with the draw inside 24 bars: stop at the reversal extreme, target the draw, 24h hold. Result: +0.043R vs matched control, CI [-0.061, +0.145], MDE 0.147 (n=793 is too few).

1H gold FVGs that overlap a Rauf-style mitigation block (52% of 11,038 FVGs). Fill-through-far-edge rate within about 120 1H bars vs the 5 nearest-distance non-overlap FVGs in ±30 days: about 88.6% vs 89.7%, diff -1.1pp, CI [-2.2, -0.1]pp, halves agree, powered. This is only a candidate EDGE: the effect is tiny, p=0.04 will not survive Holm/BH, and overlap gaps come after V-shaped legs, so the setup context may confound the result.

Reading (a), the mirrored curve. A respected left-side 4H order block before a confirmed 4H swing is broken by a close on the return leg. The first 1H retrace into the band is traded as the re-polarised block: stop beyond the zone, 2R, 48h hold. Result: +0.002R vs control, CI [-0.076, +0.083], MDE 0.114.

Reading (b), old gaps. Book: 3,868 4H FVG retests, traded as a reaction from the approach side (stop at the far edge, 2R, 48h). Old retests (traded into, 2 or more bars of accumulation, departed, then retouched within 60 days; 49% of the book) are compared with fresh first touches. Old minus fresh = -0.030R, CI [-0.117, +0.066], MDE 0.131.

Needs footprint / market-delta (aggressor-signed volume). The certified M1 data is OHLC only with no volume column, and OANDA spot gold has no exchange tape, so delta divergence cannot be computed. An OHLC proxy would be testing a different indicator.

Target reading. Untaken 1h equal-high/low pools (consecutive 2/2 swings within a declared tolerance of 0.10xATR14) were reached within 3 trading days 84.7% of the time, against 82.7% for a level at the same distance and the same NY clock time. Powered, CI contains 0.

'Do not trade away from equal highs' reading, run as a gate on the phase-3 1h CISD book. Reversals whose extreme is equal to the previous same-side swing (8% of the book) came in -0.048R vs the rest, in the claimed direction but not significant. MDE 0.156 is above 0.10, so the test is underpowered.

Gate on the 1h CISD book: the reversal extreme took PDH/PDL. The previous-week extremes are nested inside that, and it is the attested default relevant-level set. The gate fired on 23% of the book; gated minus complement was +0.025R [-0.032, +0.080]. Powered NULL.

Gate on the 1h CISD book: the reversal extreme took an untaken 1h swing formed inside the three-daily-candle window, the relevant-swing lookback. The gate fired on 21% of the book; result +0.031R [-0.028, +0.089]. Powered NULL.

After a 1h FVG is tagged and respected, does price reach the nearest untaken 2/2 swing (from the last 72 bars) within 3 trading days? It did 74.5% of the time, against 74.4% for a level at the same distance and the same clock time. Powered NULL. Only one reading was run because the variant restates the definition and makes no separate claim.

Forex Asia (20-00 NY) and London (02-05 NY) highs and lows, reached before 12:00 NY: 71.2% vs a null of 71.6% at the same distance and the same NY minute (+/-30 min, +/-30 days). Asia levels hit 73.1%, London 69.3%. Powered NULL. The two displacement rules need an undefined displacement measure and were not tested.

Still-untaken 2- and 3-day-old daily highs/lows, reached during the next session: 19.3% vs a null of 19.9% at the same distance, measured from other session opens. Powered NULL. The 1-day-old level is covered by previous-period-high-low.

Draw reading: PDH/PDL reached during the next session 46.8% of the time, against 48.6% for a level at the same distance from the session open on another day within +/-30 days. The CI excludes 0 against the claim. PDH/PDL are slightly LESS likely to be reached than an arbitrary equidistant level.

Reversal-case reading: day D-1 swept one side of D-2 and closed back inside, and D-2's opposite extreme is the target on day D. It was reached 29.2% of the time vs a null of 31.3%. Powered NULL (MDE 0.046 <= 0.05).

The central-bank hedging story can't be seen in price data, so I tested what it predicts for trading. On 1H charts (lowest low of 48 bars splits the curve), every up-close candle on the sell side was extended as a mitigation block. First M1 return after a close above the block: long, stop at block low, 2R, 10h, clustered by model. Result: +0.047R vs control, CI [-0.005, +0.100], powered NULL.

Used real CFTC COT data for COMEX gold (088691). At each quarter start: commercial net above the midpoint of its 12-month range = bullish, below = bearish. Gated a daily book with one long and one short every day (1 ATR stop, 2R, one trading day), clustered by quarter. Result: -0.013R, CI [-0.061, +0.036]. Only 43 quarters, so effective n is 43 and the test is UNDERPOWERED.

$niper's 15m sell/buy model, second-leg ('silver bullet') entries. Sequence: prior-day high/low sweep, MSS within 4h, first bearish FVG in premium, retrace entry, BOS below the leg low, first premium FVG of the second leg; target the prior-day low. The full sequence completed only 8 times in 10.5 years. n<30, so the harness rule makes it UNTESTABLE.
Tested the claim that the second leg beats the first post-MSS entry, as a gate on 134 first-leg plus 8 second-leg entries, clustered by model. The gated arm has only n=8, below 30, so UNTESTABLE.

Gate on the canonical 1h bare-CISD book (2R, 10h). Pass = the reversal extreme took the prior-day low/high and that level sits in discount/premium of the prior week's range. Gated n=1,355 (17%). Result: +0.014R, CI [-0.050, +0.078], powered NULL (MDE 0.092).

Components reading, 15m. Required: the extreme swept the prior-day low/high, a CISD close, an inversion (close through the last opposing FVG) and a 1/1 short-term low within 8 bars. Stop at the extreme, 2R, 150 min. Result: -0.024R, CI [-0.060, +0.015], powered NULL.

Finessee_Fx's 'always at a HTF PD array' claim, as a gate on the bare 15m CISD book. Pass = the extreme sits inside an unmitigated same-side daily FVG or daily order block no more than 60 days old. Gated 27.8% of the book. Result: -0.007R, CI [-0.037, +0.024], powered NULL.

1H breaker: low, high, lower low, then a body close above the up-close run into the high. Entry on the return into the block when fair value coincides (FVG overlap or the leg's 50% inside the block). Stop at the lower low, 2R, 10h. Result: +0.030R, CI [-0.011, +0.071], powered NULL.

Daily chart, as the source says. Tested whether price clears the original consolidation (5-day range <= 1.5 ATR, breakout, then a daily CISD SMR beyond it) within 20 trading days. Null = same distance and horizon at matched random times. Hit rate beat the 62.1% null by +3.7pp, CI [-6.0, +12.8]pp, n=114: UNDERPOWERED.

Variant B on 4H (forex grid) and 1D: C2 takes C1's extreme and closes beyond it, then C3 closes through the series open (a CISD). Entry at the C3 close, stop at the C2/C3 extreme, 2R. Diff +0.036R, CI [-0.059, +0.125]; MDE 0.131, so it is short of power.

Variant A: a lower-timeframe CISD (4H with 15m, 1D with 1H) inside an unfinished HTF C2 whose swing is beyond C1's extreme. Stop at the protected swing, 2R. Diff +0.002R, CI [-0.020, +0.024]. Powered NULL. Before any test of b I changed the pairing from 4H/1H and 1D/4H: a 2/2 1H CISD cannot confirm inside one 4H candle, so 4H/1H gave zero events.

5m CISD book limited to moments where the pre-open bias (previous daily candle) and the same-day dynamic bias (15m close through a 2/2 swing, with an FVG on the leg) disagree. Trading with the dynamic bias vs the pre-open bias: diff +0.002R, CI [-0.025, +0.029]. Powered NULL; the gate fired on 50% of events.

Toolkit tested through its FVG array: first M1 return into a 1h FVG, stop at the far edge, target the most recent 1h swing on the far side (the old high/low), hold 10h. Diff +0.093R, CI [-0.020, +0.226]. The far targets make R highly variable (MDE 0.176), so it is short of power.

First 1h close at least 3 ATR14 from the 21 EMA; does price touch the EMA within 1,440 M1 bars? Hit 26.0% vs 26.2% for a same-distance null, diff -0.003, CI [-0.036, +0.032]. Powered NULL. Timeframe, ATR period and horizon were declared before the run.

Baseline: 5m FVG first-return trades (2R, 50 min hold). Gate: the gap overlaps a live same-direction 10m or 15m FVG at the decision. Diff +0.019R, CI [-0.001, +0.038], gate rate 30%. Powered NULL. This is the second run: the first checked overlap when the 5m gap formed, not when price returned to it (gate rate 3.9%, diff +0.038, also NULL). I found the bug after seeing that verdict, re-ran once, and both runs are in the ledger and the notes.

5m pattern: a 3h box (range at most 4x the mean bar range), a close beyond it, a 30-min second box at most half the first's range, then a breakout close. Stop at the second box, 2R. Only 103 events under the knobs declared before the run; diff -0.096R, CI [-0.38, +0.19].

Two-model trade. Sponsor: a live 4H FVG, which fails on a 4H close beyond its far edge. Execution: the first 5m CISD whose swing is inside the gap. Stop at that swing, target the most recent 4H swing (the sponsor's liquidity), hold 40h, one trade per array. Diff +0.034R, CI [-0.085, +0.154]; MDE 0.171.

Order-pairing range with both required confirmations: the first 1h C2 closure through PDH or PDL, plus XAG_USD SMT (silver has not taken its own prior-day extreme). Target the opposite side of the range, hold 24h, control matched on NY time of day. Diff -0.166R, CI [-0.46, +0.14]; only n=282. The two FVG frameworks have no rule for picking the key gap, so they were not run (see notes).
Candle-3 stack gate (last closed daily AND last closed 4H bar are C2s in the trade direction) on the 15m rung-0 CISD book. Gated 1,998 vs complement 30,731: +0.001R [-0.051,+0.055]. Powered null.

Live expansion-support gate: the in-progress daily and 4H candles are both beyond their open in the trade direction, with opposing run <= 1.0 x body. Tested on the 15m CISD book: +0.008R [-0.021,+0.038]. Powered null.

Full four-part checklist: daily C3, 4H C4, previous-day extreme not yet taken, 15m CISD. Stop at the protected swing, target the previous-day extreme with a 2R floor, hold to the daily close. 174 trades, +0.35R vs control; the CI excludes 0 but the MDE is 0.46, far below the power floor. Candidate only. This is the re-run after one bug fix; the first run (+0.47R) is recorded in the notes.
4H route: bias from a daily C2 plus an H1 CISD inside it; a 4H C2 inside the C3 day (no POI); first 15m CISD inside the 4H C3; 2R; hold to the 4H close. +0.004R [-0.059,+0.066]. Powered null.

1H route: same daily bias; a 1H C2 at a POI (an untaken 1H swing or an untouched 1H FVG within 72 bars); first 5m CISD inside the 1H C3; 2R; hold to the 1H close. +0.015R [-0.052,+0.093]. MDE 0.104 is just above the 0.10 threshold.

D/1H/5m model: a 5m raid below PDL (or above PDH) inside the London or NY AM killzone, then an MSS within 60min, then a 5m FVG. Entry on the retrace to the FVG top; stop at the raid extreme; fixed 2R; hold to the daily close. 227 trades, +0.12R [-0.06,+0.32]. Underpowered.

Flowchart as one reading: daily C2 bias; the 5m extreme reaches an untouched 1H FVG (IRL) or takes an untaken 1H swing (ERL); 5m stop raid plus CISD, both in the London or NY AM killzone; 2R; hold to the daily close. 425 trades, +0.02R [-0.11,+0.17]. Underpowered.

Worked MMXM sell/buy trade: sweep of PDH, a 5m CISD reversal at the day's high, entry on the retrace to the 50% premium of the dealing range. Stop at the manipulation high, target PDL (the 'original consolidation'), mirrored for buys, held to the daily close. 1,610 trades, +0.14R [-0.02,+0.31]. MDE 0.23, underpowered.

Curve reading (sell side, then smart-money reversal, then buy side, with zones dragged across) is UNTESTABLE. The source never defines the curve's phases, gives no rule for which side price is on (method_spec §3.9 GAP), and never says which zones to drag forward or how many.

Consolidation = the day after an inside day (range = mother candle). Gate: 15m CISD entries in the outer 25% of the range, pointing back inward, vs all other in-range entries (523 vs 3,537). -0.157R [-0.270,-0.041]. Both halves are negative; ties are negligible.

Session AMD: a London excursion beyond one side of the Asia range, then a 15m CISD closing back inside the range. Target the opposite Asia extreme; stop at the manipulation extreme. 764 trades, -0.017R [-0.10,+0.07]. MDE 0.124, underpowered.

Candle-level AMD on the 18:00 daily open: manipulation beyond the open, then a 15m CISD from the day's extreme closing back through the open. Target the -2SD projection of the manipulation leg. +0.016R [-0.035,+0.070]. Powered null.

Friday branch: Tue and Wed expand with no internal swing, then Thursday prints a daily C2 plus an hourly CISD; trade Friday toward the weekly open with the stop beyond Thursday's extreme. Only 35 weeks qualify, so the test is underpowered. Re-run once with hold_basis=bars per README trap 7 because clock-run exposure differed by 14%.

Thursday-intraday branch: enter at the first hourly CISD after Wednesday's extreme is swept, target the weekly open, hold to Friday's close. n=52, underpowered. Re-run once with hold_basis=bars per trap 7 because clock-run exposure differed by 18%.

Gate on the 15m bare-CISD book: the confirming bar also takes out the latest unbroken 2/2 swing extreme. Claim '-'; the difference points the claimed way but the CI contains 0 and the test is powered (MDE 0.041).

Gate on the 15m bare-CISD book: the previous day's high/low objective was already taken before the entry. Claim '-'; the difference points the claimed way but the CI contains 0 and the test is powered (MDE 0.042).

Daily C3 (yesterday was a C2) and London 02-05 holds the day's extreme; enter on a 15m continuation CISD (higher low) closing 06:00-09:30 NY, stop at the protected swing, target the previous day's high/low, flat at 17:00. n=175, underpowered.
Same as reading a, but C4 days are also allowed (yesterday was a C3 closing beyond the C2's extreme). The difference is negative but underpowered (MDE 0.32).

After a daily C2, buy the first dip below the 18:00 open (before 10:30, still above the previous day's EQ), stop at the EQ, target the previous day's high (mirror for shorts). The difference is negative but the test is underpowered (MDE 0.13). Re-run once with hold_basis=bars per trap 7 (clock run: -0.068 [-0.156, +0.026], exposure gap 15%).

Gate: among bias-direction 15m CISDs that turn at the day's extreme, keep only those whose extreme formed before 10:30 NY. The gate fires on 93% of trades, so the complement is thin: effective n is 105 and the test is underpowered.

Full playbook: a daily C2/C3 closure confirmed by an hourly CISD, then an hourly C2 in the previous day's bias-side half, then a 5m CISD within the next hour; 2R target, 50-minute hold. The difference is negative and underpowered (MDE 0.119), consistent with phase 3's refuted 5m/1H/1D conjunction.
Seek-and-destroy day (both Asia extremes taken): fade every 15m deviation that closes back inside the Asia range, stop at the deviation extreme, target rung 1 (the range EQ). Powered and NULL.

Same deviations as reading a, targeting rung 3 (the opposite Asia boundary). CI contains 0 and MDE is 0.113 against the 0.10 threshold, so underpowered. Rung 2 (OTE) was not tested because the leg is unspecified.

Gate on the 15m bare-CISD book: the last completed daily candle is an inside day. Claim '-' (worse), but gated trades came out 0.044R better, with the CI excluding 0 and both halves positive: NEGATIVE, p=0.021. Unlikely to survive campaign-wide Holm.

Gate on the 15m bare-CISD book: the last three completed 4H closes (forex grid) all sit inside the range of the 4H candle before them. Claim '-', but gated trades came out 0.041R better: NEGATIVE, p=0.013. Correlated with reading a.

An inventory of what is on the chart; the corpus itself calls the refusals personal preference. There is no directional price claim, and its only measurable is a no-difference comparison against an unspecified set, which a +/- verdict cannot express. The kept and dropped tools are each tested under their own ids.

A list of design exclusions with no directional price claim; its only measurable is a signal count. Several items need data the harness lacks (order flow, DOM, TPO) or are venue choices (futures vs CFD). Each excluded tool is tested under its own id.

Gate test on the sequential 15m bare-CISD book: the first 3 trades of each trading day vs the 4th and later trades the cap rules out. Powered NULL, +0.022R [-0.009, +0.053], MDE 0.044. Re-run twice to fix bugs in _book.py; the notes record both earlier runs, and both were also NULL.

The guest gives no numbers, so limits were declared before the run: stop for the day at -2R/+4R or after 3 losses or 3 wins in a row, and for the week at -5R/+10R. Trades taken while no limit is active vs trades after a limit fires: powered NULL, +0.004R [-0.026, +0.033]. Same two bug-fix re-runs as the first concept, noted in the result.
Reading a, stop after the second loss of the day ($niper / Trader T): trades before the second daily loss vs trades after it. Powered NULL, +0.012R [-0.019, +0.042].
Reading b, at most 1 trade a day and 2 a week (the variant definition): the gated arm has only 1,101 trades. MDE 0.107 is above the 0.10 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED, +0.038R [-0.037, +0.113].

The guest describes about 8 trades a week as what his discretionary MMXM model on indices and BTC happens to produce, and says outright it is not an enforced cap. There is no decision rule to put on a gold book, and a cap test would test a claim he does not make. The cap readings are tested under the other two frequency concepts.

Reading a, size down after an extended winning run (declared as 3 winners in a row), claim '-'. Trades after the run come out slightly better, not worse, and the CI contains 0: powered NULL, +0.037R [-0.026, +0.098]. The 'would tilt you' trigger is subjective and was not tested. Same bug-fix re-runs, noted in the result.

Reading b, size down when volatility has risen: mean 15m true range over the last day at or above 1.5x its 20-day mean (declared), claim '-'. Powered NULL, -0.009R [-0.079, +0.058], MDE 0.098. This probe is the one that caught both _book.py bugs.

Reading a, Ash's no-break-even rule. BE and fixed differ only on trades that reach +1R and then come back to entry before the target, so the test scores holding the original stop and target from that retest. Candidate EDGE, +0.046R [+0.003, +0.089], halves +0.063/+0.030; fixed minus BE on affected trades is +0.038R gross. Not robust: 37 retest bars that also hit the original stop were dropped (fixed loses -1R there). Putting them back would lower the diff by about 0.011R and take the CI's low end below 0. p=0.036, so it is unlikely to survive Holm/BH.

Reading b, Ash's no-trim rule. The test scores the position held from the first +1R tag with the original stop and target. Weak NEGATIVE, -0.012R [-0.023, -0.0005], p=0.041, gross -0.007R: holding past +1R does slightly worse than a random entry with the same geometry, so trimming there does not lose value. Borderline, and unlikely to survive multiplicity correction.

The ladder can only beat flat 1% sizing if trades after a win do better than trades after a loss, so that is the test (gate: previous taken trade won, claim '+'). Powered NULL, -0.025R [-0.055, +0.006], leaning the wrong way. Sizing off the last outcome adds variance, not expectancy, on this book.

Pure capital structure and sizing with a psychological rationale: deposit only what you can lose, never top up, withdraw the initial, then size up on the rest. It changes neither which trades are taken nor how they exit ('same model at larger size'), so no OHLC outcome can decide it. The withdrawal trigger and the size-up multiple are not stated either.

15m CISD entries targeting the nearest session level beyond price (Asia or London H/L, 08:30 NY open, PDH/PDL) that is at least 1.5R away. No trade if that level is over 3R or beyond the remaining 5-day ADR. Powered NULL, -0.012R [-0.037, +0.013]. 45% of trades time out at the declared 150-min hold.

Gate on the 1h CISD book. The week's anchor is its first 1h CISD leg. Trades in the anchor's direction are blocked once price reaches the -4 SD projection (1,841 blocked). Allowed minus blocked is +0.036R [-0.032, +0.104], NULL and powered.

Rauf reading on the 1h CISD book: trade only when the last month and the last week both closed beyond the prior period's high or low (27% of events pass). -0.021R [-0.083, +0.038]. The month-clustered CI leaves an effective n of 59, so it is UNDERPOWERED.

Daily-draw reading (Jokerszn/Nick close-through test) on the 1h CISD book: trade only after the prior day closed beyond the day-before's high or low. Allowed trades did worse than those taken on an inside-close day: -0.064R [-0.113, -0.011], NEGATIVE.

Longs only in the 1h CISD book. Blocked when the 2R target sits above the running ATH, taken as the larger of the pre-sample 1921.17 and the in-data maximum (301 blocked). +0.033R [-0.102, +0.159]. Only 187 effective days, so UNDERPOWERED.
The rule picks between NQ and ES futures by relative volatility and weekly relative weakness. The dataset is single-instrument XAUUSD, so there is no second series to choose between.

Tight-stop profile on 5m CISD entries, which stand in for the order-flow entry: stop 0.0625% of price (2.5 ES points), target 3.2R, 50-minute hold. avg_R -0.050 against a matched random entry: -0.013R [-0.024, -0.003], NEGATIVE. Ties are negligible.

NFP only, with dates from the BLS reference-week rule (95% show an 08:30 volatility spike). Blocked: the pre-NFP days of the week, NFP day before 08:30, and any hold that spans the release. Allowed minus blocked is -0.065R [-0.141, +0.013]. MDE 0.110, so UNDERPOWERED; the point estimate runs against the claim.
Gate on the 15m CISD book: block entries whose decision close sits at 0.40-0.60 of the prior day's range. Allowed minus blocked is -0.011R [-0.046, +0.025], NULL and powered (MDE 0.051).
Gate on the 1h CISD book: allowed only once the current trading day has taken the previous day's high or low (a daily Strat '1' is not yet resolved). -0.003R [-0.058, +0.050], NULL and powered.

Gate on the 1h CISD book: block trades in the direction of a run of three or more same-direction daily candle bodies (11% blocked). +0.062R [-0.023, +0.150]. MDE 0.124, so UNDERPOWERED; the sign agrees with the claim.

This is option-premium arithmetic. Scoring it needs 0DTE chain data (premium, IV, bid/ask, theta) and only the underlying's OHLC exists. The underlying's entry and target belong to the separate chart-setup concepts.

Gate on the 15m rung-0 CISD book. Blocked trades are entries in the same direction as the day's move once the day's range reaches 80% of the median of the last 3 real days. Kept vs blocked (complement n=4,525): -0.012R, CI [-0.048, +0.021]. Powered (MDE 0.049), so NULL.

Gate on the 15m CISD book. Blocked trades are entries in the direction of a run of 3 or more consecutive daily expansion candles (opposing run/|body| <= 1.0). +0.011R, CI [-0.060, +0.085]. Only 1,164 blocked trades (effective n 192), MDE 0.104, so UNDERPOWERED.
Same gate with a 2-day expansion streak (the 'after two days, wait for a new phase' corollary). +0.016R, CI [-0.026, +0.061]. Powered (MDE 0.062), so NULL.

Rate test, claim '-'. On gap days (|open - prev close| >= 0.25 ADR20), does price reach a full ADR move from the open against the gap? The null uses random non-gap days within +/-30d at the same distance and direction. 15.7% vs 15.4%. Only 70 gap days on gold, MDE 13.7pp, so UNDERPOWERED.

Rate test, claim '-'. At 09:30 NY, untaken 15m swing targets with an untaken protected swing (one beyond its 2 preceding swings) between them and price. Same-day hit rate 12.3% vs 13.3% for a null at the same distance, side and bar count (09:30 on random days within +/-30d). -0.99pp, CI [-1.7, -0.3]pp, both halves negative, powered (MDE 1.0pp). Only a candidate EDGE, pending Holm/BH. The effect is small (about 7% relative). A guarded target by construction sits behind a higher low (or lower high) that is still holding, so this may be trend persistence rather than anything specific to the protected swing.

Gate on the 15m CISD book. 'Consolidating' means a completed day's range contains the 2 or more real days after it (inside-days box, searching back up to 20 days) and today has not yet taken either side of it; about 8% of entries. Outside vs inside: +0.006R, CI [-0.041, +0.052]. Powered, so NULL.

Same gate with the 'small days, small bodies' box: 3 real days, each with range < ADR20 and body <= 0.5 x range, and today still inside their combined range; about 5% of entries. -0.013R, CI [-0.086, +0.056]. Effective n 179, MDE 0.101, so UNDERPOWERED.

Gate on the 15m CISD book. A stop is untrusted when its protected swing forms a near-equal pair with another same-side swing (within 0.10 x ATR14, previous 20 bars). Trusted vs equal-pair stops: -0.001R, CI [-0.039, +0.036]. Powered, so NULL. SMT could not be computed because there are no gold-in-EUR/GBP series, so all equal pairs are treated as having no SMT.

UNTESTABLE. Defines how prop firms compute drawdown (static, EOD-trailing, unrealised-trailing, DLL + MLL). These are contract definitions with no claim about XAUUSD price. Breach probability depends on a strategy's P&L path under firm terms, not on OHLC.

UNTESTABLE. Futures feed settings: back-adjust, settlement, ETH/RTH, minis vs micros. The certified data is a single spot XAUUSD series with no contract rolls, settlement price or mini/micro pair, so neither side of any toggle exists. The NY timezone setting is already the settled harness convention.

UNTESTABLE. Chooses between vehicles: futures chart vs ETF/options/CFD, minis vs micros. Only one instrument series exists (spot gold, already including overnight), so there is no second vehicle to compare levels, signals or fills against.

Trade test on 15m bars with 2/2 fractal swings. The flip is a close beyond the last valid swing against the previous break. Entry at the flip close, stop at the strong extreme, 2R target, 10h hold. Result -0.011R vs the matched random entry: powered NULL (MDE 0.034). Probe passed, ties negligible.

Trade test on 15m bars. A failure swing is a lower swing high that retraces at least 70% of the prior leg. It is confirmed by a close below the swing bar's low within 8 bars. Stop at the failure-swing extreme, target the lows that produced it (the draw), 24h hold. Result -0.019R vs control: powered NULL (MDE 0.040).

Gate test on the 15m first-flip plus second-break book, with identical stop and 2R trades, clustered by flip. The gate is the second continuation break. Result -0.022R vs the first flip: powered NULL (MDE 0.063). The HTF key-area split the speaker leaves open was not tested.

Gate test. Baseline is the first 15m close back through the 4H candle's opening price (the breaker), with stop at the candle extreme so far, 2R and a 4h hold. The gate asks whether a turtle soup, then an order-block confirmation, came first inside the candle (29% of events). Result +0.024R: powered NULL (MDE 0.077).

Rate test. Does the next 4H candle's high or low fall inside an active 4H or 1D array (FVG or order block) fixed at the prior 4H close? Observed 60.0% vs a null of 59.6%. The null uses the same % offset from the open against a random other candle's arrays within +/-30d. Powered NULL (MDE 2.2pp). The 'every wick' claim also fails outright: 40% of extremes sit in no array.

Gate test on 1h STRAT runs of 2 or more same-direction 2s that reverse with an opposite 2. Stop at the run extreme, target the base of the stack, 24h hold. The gate is a run of 5 or more (8% of 5,297 events, 421 gated). Result +0.097R, CI [-0.13, +0.33]: UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.325). Locked at 1h, so no re-run on 15m.

The taxonomy is definitional, so only 'a 2 is trending' was scored. Trade every closed 1h 2 in its direction, stop at its opposite extreme, 1R, 10h hold. Result +0.003R, CI [-0.007, +0.014]. The CI would read NULL, but 36% of control draws are the concept's own trades (the book fires on about 60% of hourly closes), so the harness labels it UNDERPOWERED. The 'a 3 fails early' tendency was not scored: it has no threshold and no null that isolates it.

Rule tested: after 3 or more consecutive daily expansion closures, a continuation trade is worse (claim '-'). Run as a gate on the daily continuation book (next-session open, stop at the day's EQ (midpoint of the range), target the day's extreme). Only 124 gated trades against 1,026 in the complement; the diff is +0.05R, opposite to the claim, but the CI is wide and the MDE is 0.31R.

Rule tested: a daily expansion met by an opposite daily expansion is a reversal; trade away from the two-day wick with a 2R target and a 5-session hold. 127 trades, +0.03R versus the matched control; n < 200, so the verdict cannot be NULL. This is run 2 of 2: run 1 used ctrl_tod_tol_min=30, which left 60 of 127 trades with no control draw. I re-ran once with ctrl_grid=1D and recorded this in the notes.

Consolidation defined as no 1h close beyond the latest 2/2 swing in the last 24 bars (absence of displacement), used as a gate on the phase-3 1h CISD book, claim '-'. The gate fired on only 0.7% of events (55 of 8,033), so the test cannot decide.

Range = a 1h mother bar plus 3 inside bars. The side taken first sets the direction; entry on a 5m close back inside the range, stop at the sweep extreme, target the opposite side. 2,184 trades at +0.02R versus control. The 18% win rate makes the R variance large, giving an MDE of 0.22R. The halves disagree (H1 +0.22, H2 -0.18).

Reading b: the bias selects which side must be run. Tested as a gate on the reading-a book: trades aligned with the daily previous-candle bias versus the rest. 756 aligned trades at -0.17R, against the claim, but the CI is wide (MDE 0.45R).

Claim: a failed closure through the opposing series (no series_open close within 3 1h bars) means the swing extreme is taken before the far side of the range. Hit rate 56.4% against a geometry-matched null of 55.8%, diff +0.7pp. The test is powered (MDE 2.3pp), so this is a well-powered zero.

Half-candle timing rider: on the phase-3 1h CISD book, closures whose first M1 close-through comes in the first half of the confirming candle versus later ones (claim '+'). Timely closures are -0.068R, against the claim (p=0.07). Both halves are negative. The complement has only 1,117 trades, so the MDE is 0.105, just over the 0.10 threshold.

Baseline: continuation trades after a 4h (forex grid) expansion candle, with a 2R target and a 40h hold in trading bars. Gate: the next candle is an inside bar, the HTF consolidation signature. 1,527 gated trades at -0.036R; MDE 0.116, just short of power.

Same 4h book. Gate: the next candle closes back inside the expansion candle's range (a small-range consolidation or retracement), versus further expansion or expansion met with expansion. -0.007R; powered, MDE 0.093.

Order-of-extremes tie-breaker: on daily closes that land back inside the prior day's range, a high made before the low (on M1) means bearish for the next session, and vice versa. The day's extremes are used as stop and target. Diff -0.003R with CI +/-0.06. It would have been NULL, but the daily control grid put 27% of control draws on the concept's own trades (ctrl_overlap > 20%), so the harness forces UNDERPOWERED.

Rule: a doji daily close gives no bias. Tested as a gate (body <= 10% of range, declared before the run) on the previous-candle daily bias book, claim '-'. 174 doji trades at -0.06R, the direction the claim predicts but not significant. n < 200.

Book: 15m closes beyond 2/2 swings, window of 4 bars, stop at the window extreme, 2R, 150min hold. Gate: the threshold_fits magnitude test (range ratio >= 1.5 and distance ratio >= 0.65), which fired on 39% of breaks. +0.015R; powered, MDE 0.048.
Same book. Gate: FVG required, meaning a same-direction 3-bar FVG inside the N=4 window. It fired on 62% of breaks, matching threshold_fits' 61%. +0.011R; powered, MDE 0.051.

Path test. Baseline: 1,030 one-sided daily C2s, entered at the next open, stop at the C2 extreme, target at the C2's opposite extreme, held one trading day. Gate: the candle made its low before its high (open-low-high-close), checked on M1. -0.056R, CI [-0.195, +0.086]; effective n 378, so it is badly underpowered.
Shape test on the same daily C2 book. Gate: opposing run larger than the body (large wick, small body). +0.041R, CI [-0.061, +0.150], MDE 0.15. The daily sample is too small to decide.

4H candle with a 15m CISD. Baseline: 14,795 CISDs whose protected swing is the 4h candle's running wick, 2R, 10 bars. Gate 'trusted': the extreme formed in the first 25% of the candle and the opposing run is at most 0.30 of the prior candle's range; it fires on 30.5%. -0.004R, CI [-0.043, +0.033], a powered null.
1D candle with a 1h CISD, same trusted-wick gate, 3,910 events, gate fires on 43.8%. +0.050R, CI [-0.028, +0.126], MDE 0.110, just short of the power threshold.

FVG as an entry array. On the first return to a 1h FVG's near edge within 1,440 M1 bars, enter in the gap's direction, stop beyond the far edge, 2R, 10h hold. Against a matched control: +0.025R, CI [-0.009, +0.059], a powered null (MDE 0.048).

FVG as a draw. The 1h FVG is fully filled (price reaches the far edge) within 1,440 M1 bars 75.9% of the time, against 74.9% for a level at the same distance and on the same side at matched random moments. +1.0pp, CI [+0.0004, +0.020], p=0.044. This is only a candidate EDGE: the lower bound barely clears 0, it would not survive Holm/BH, and it may reflect volatility clustering right after a displacement rather than a draw. The null matches the ±30-day regime but not local volatility.

Earliest-recordings MSS on 15m. A close through a lower high (or a higher low), where the displacing leg left an FVG. Enter on the first return to that FVG within 16 bars, stop at the leg extreme, 2R, 150min hold. +0.001R, CI [-0.042, +0.042], a powered null.

Later-canon MSS on 15m. The leg first sweeps the last swing low (stop raid), then price closes through the swing high. Enter on the first return to 50% of the displacement range within 16 bars, stop at the swept extreme, 2R. -0.002R, CI [-0.036, +0.034], a powered null.

1h order block, structural validation. A 2/2 extreme raids the last confirmed swing. The opposing-close run into it is validated by a close through the run's far extreme (low of the up-close run, high of the down-close run) within 3 bars. Retest the block's opening price within 24h, stop at the extreme, 2R, 10h. +0.031R, CI [-0.024, +0.088], a powered null (MDE 0.080).

1h order block, candle/propulsion validation. Same raid and retest as reading a, but validated by a close through the run's opening price (the series_open CISD). +0.053R, CI [+0.006, +0.100], p=0.028. Both halves agree (H1 +0.057, H2 +0.049) and the tie shares match. Only a candidate EDGE: p=0.028 is unlikely to survive campaign-wide Holm/BH.

Baseline: 4,559 continuation trades. Each is the first 5m CISD after a pullback inside a confirmed 1h impulse leg (a close through a swing), stop at the pullback extreme, 2R. Gate: pullback depth below 0.618 of the leg (74% shallow, median depth 0.43). +0.057R, CI [-0.017, +0.129], MDE 0.104, effective n 1,016. The sign is right but the test is just short of power.

Wick reading. Baseline: 3,978 1h CISDs taken in the direction of the previous daily candle's close, stop at the protected swing, 2R. Gate: the day's running low has held the previous day's 50% level (EQ) (fires 52.6%). -0.042R, against the claim but inside CI [-0.118, +0.038], MDE 0.112.
Close reading on the same book. Gate: no 1h close of the day beyond the previous day's EQ, against the trade (fires 61.9%). -0.027R, CI [-0.103, +0.053], MDE 0.112.

Baseline: 16,184 4h candles (forex grid), each traded in its close direction from the next open with ±1 ATR(20) barriers and a 3-candle hold in trading time. Gate: body at least as large as the opposing run, i.e. not a reversal candle (fires 64.8%). -0.009R, CI [-0.040, +0.021]. A powered null: body larger than wick does not predict expansion.

Tested 4h forex-grid close-direction continuation (1 ATR barrier, rr 1, 3 candles), gated on 'not large': a candle is large only if both opposing run/range > 0.30 AND time-to-extreme share > 0.25. Result is a powered zero (NULL).
Same 4h book, gated on the time axis alone: time share to the opposing extreme <= 0.25 of the candle's traded span. NULL, powered.

Live reading: measured at the 4h candle midpoint (open + 120 min). Trade the side of the open, stop at the opposing extreme so far, exit at the candle close. Gate: opposing run so far / range so far <= 0.30. EDGE candidate at +0.041R, but the CI low end is +0.0004 and p = 0.049, so it is borderline and unlikely to survive Holm/BH.
Baseline is the phase-3 rung-0 15m CISD. Gate: the in-progress 1D, 4H and 1H candles all support the trade by wick geometry (price beyond the open and opposing run <= body so far). NULL, powered.

Same 15m CISD baseline. Gate: 'all timeframes green', meaning price is beyond the open of the in-progress 1D, 4H and 1H candles in the trade direction. NULL, powered; the point estimate is +0.024R and the CI just touches 0.

TTrades gating claim: bare 5m inversions (a full close beyond the far edge within 12 bars; stop at the swing point; 2R; 50 min) versus those inside a live 1H C2 that swept the previous 1H extreme and has a small wick. NULL, powered: the gate adds nothing.

Canonical retest: 15m inversion, then the first M1 return to the inverted zone's near edge within 4h. Stop at the swing point, 2R, 150 min, against a matched random entry. EDGE candidate at +0.018R, p = 0.033; small and near the Holm/BH line.

15m volume imbalance (close-to-open gap >= 0.10 ATR with overlapping ranges), traded on the first M1 return to the near edge within 4h. Stop at the far edge +/- 0.25 ATR, 2R, 150 min. The locked rule says EDGE (+0.039R), but 94% of events fall in 2016-2020 (H2 n = 943). In 2016-2018 the M1 feed's median open-to-previous-close jump was about 5x larger (~0.10 vs ~0.02 later), so most of these volume imbalances come from the feed, not the market. Treat this result as depending on the feed era; the caveat is in the result's notes.

Baseline: 5m structure breaks with displacement (threshold_fits N=4, r=1.5, d=0.65), traded in the reversal direction. Gate: the 15m structure is still intact in the original trend; claim '-' (those should be mere pullbacks). NULL, powered: the 15m hierarchy makes no difference. Re-run once after a bug fix; the first run emitted 0 events because a stop-side check was inverted. A data-hole guard was also added before any test ran.

Baseline is the rung-0 5m CISD. Gate: the opposing series traded into a level known before it began: a live trade-polarity 1H FVG (<= 72h old), a sweep of an untaken 1H 2/2 swing, or a sweep of the previous day's extreme. NULL, powered: the HTF level adds nothing.

Baseline: retest entries at the CISD-born block level of 5m blocks with a series of >= 2 candles (stop at the protected swing, 2R, 50 min). Gate: the series collapses into one 15m candle that closed in the series' direction. NULL, powered.

Trend = 2 consecutive days taking PDH (or PDL) by wick. Hit = the next session takes today's high (low); null = same distance and same bar horizon from random moments. 50.7% vs null 54.9%, so the trend-conditioned draw is hit LESS often than geometry predicts. Caveat: real windows start at the 18:00 reopen and the null windows do not.

15m BPR (a new FVG overlapping an opposing FVG from <=20 bars earlier; zone = the intersection), first retrace into the zone, stop at the extreme between the gaps, 2R. +0.024R vs matched control. EDGE candidate only: H1 +0.055 but H2 +0.0006 (about zero), so the effect lives in 2016-2020. Must survive Holm/BH.
Premium/discount rule (longs below the previous day's EQ, shorts above) as a gate on the reading-a BPR book: +0.033R, CI contains 0, powered NULL.

The dollar filter he rejects (the last completed EURUSD-inverted daily candle agrees with the trade), tested as a gate on 1h CISD rung 0. Powered NULL (-0.003R), which SUPPORTS the concept's claim that the dollar is not usable for gold bias. Proxy is EURUSD, not DXY.

First 15m interaction with PDH/PDL each day, sorted into the three branches by closes. Branch 3 (no close beyond) fades; branch 2 (close back inside within 3 bars) reverses; branch 1 continues. 2R, 150m hold. +0.051R, halves agree (+0.038 / +0.063). EDGE candidate, but CI low end is +0.0006 and p=0.05, a very likely Holm/BH casualty. Counts: branch 3 = 1227, branch 1 = 727, branch 2 = 610.
Post-creation rebalance: 1h FVG fully filled (M1 touch of the far edge within 5D), then trade the reversal in the gap's direction, stop 1 gap height beyond, 2R, 10h hold. +0.026R, powered NULL.

Pre-creation daily rebalance: C3 opens beyond C1's extreme but inside C2's range. Race: does C1's extreme get touched before C2's extreme? 36.9% vs geometry null 36.2%, powered NULL. The 'majority of candles' claim is not borne out either (37% raw).

London run with a 15m CISD at the London extreme that reached PDH/PDL. Does that extreme hold for the rest of the day more often than a clock-matched null? 37.8% vs 36.7%; n=209 is below the power floor.

Fake CISD: a London CISD extreme that did NOT reach PDH/PDL. Is it re-run the same day more often than a clock-matched null? 63.5% vs 65.6%, sign against the claim; n=400 is underpowered (MDE 0.072 vs 0.05).

15m 2-2 reversals (stop at the 2down/2up extreme, 2R), gated on a preceding liquidity run (the reversal bar first undercuts the latest confirmed 2/2 swing). Gated vs ungated -0.009R, powered NULL. Side note: the ungated complement beat its own control by +0.027R (p=2e-5), which is not what the concept claims.

1h CISD order blocks, each entered at both the body mean threshold and the 0.5-of-wick level (stop at the protected swing, 2R). Gate = the row uses the level the rule prescribes (wick > body -> wick 0.5). +0.028R, CI contains 0, powered NULL (MDE 0.091).

UNTESTABLE: the rule applies only to Bitcoin, a market that trades around the clock. The harness has only XAUUSD, which closes every day and at weekends (the guest's stated reason), so neither a BTC setup book nor BTC volatility by hour can be measured. Moving the rule to gold would test a different claim.

Gate on 5m bare CISD. Kept only trades where the 1H and 15m previous-candle narratives (method_spec 2.3) disagree. Trades that followed the 1H narrative did 0.042R worse than trades that followed the 15m one, CI [-0.079, -0.009]. That is against the 'hourly is the sweet spot' claim, but H1 (2016-2020) alone does not exclude 0.
Tested the 1H->5m row of the table. 5m CISD reversals whose swept extreme sits in a paired 1H FVG did the same as reversals at an adjacent 15m or 4H FVG: -0.006R [-0.031, +0.020]. Powered NULL.

Rate test: is the Monday high or low traded through by the Friday close? 70.9% against a matched null of 70.8% (same distance, same number of tradable bars, random moments within +/-30 days), rows clustered by week. Monday's extremes are no more of a liquidity target than any level at that distance. Powered NULL.

Trade test of sweep, reject, run from Tuesday to Friday. The first 1h candle through a Monday extreme that closes back inside is the entry; stop at that candle's extreme, target the opposite Monday extreme, hold to Friday 17:00 NY with hold_basis='bars'. Result: -0.318R against the matched control. The MDE is 0.38, so this is not a powered estimate; H1 is -0.10 and not significant, H2 is -0.52.
Gate on 5m bare CISD. Entries from 09:30 to 11:30 NY (DST-aware) against all other times: +0.012R [-0.012, +0.036]. Powered NULL.

Rate test over sessions in quarter-end closing weeks. Share of small-range days (range below the median of the prior 20 sessions): 45.9% against a null of 51.0% from other weeks within +/-30 days. The difference points against the dampener claim, and n=196 is too few to decide.

Same small-range-day test on every month-end closing week: 48.2% against a null of 51.7%, diff -0.035 [-0.074, +0.004]. Leans against the claim. MDE 0.056 is above the 0.05 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED.

Live reading on 5m bare CISD: the in-progress hour is a 2 in the trade's direction, against hours that are a 1 (inside). The gated trades did 0.044R worse, [-0.061, -0.027], and both halves are negative. Waiting for the hour to be a 2 means buying after the extension.
Confirmed-at-close reading: the last completed hour is a 2 in the trade's direction, against a 1. Result -0.012R [-0.035, +0.010]. Powered NULL.

Gate on a phase-3 bare 5m CISD book (50-minute hold). Gate: decision inside 08:00-10:30 NY, compared with the rest of the day. The control-adjusted difference is +0.008R, so the window has no effect. Powered (MDE 0.034). The 'ranging morning -> downgrade' clause is not quantified in the corpus and was not tested.

Pure-clock rate test, paired by day. Step-up = the 15-minute M1 range after T is larger than the 15 minutes before. The claim for forex-class gold is that 08:30 is the time level and 09:30 is not. Step-up rate is 57.4% at 08:30 against 73.6% at 09:30, so 09:30 is clearly the bigger volatility step on gold and the asset-class claim is contradicted. Caveat: the 08:15-08:30 'before' window contains the 08:20 COMEX gold open, which raises the 08:30 baseline. Also, the null here is the 09:30 comparator, not a random-time null.

Tests the 08:30 step-up on NFP days (dates from the BLS rule; the only news calendar that can be derived) against 08:30 on random non-NFP weekdays within +/-30 days. 97.6% against 56.7%: a large and obvious effect, but only 123 NFP days exist, below the 200 effective-n floor, so the verdict is UNDERPOWERED by construction. This is a volatility fact, not a trading edge.

Respect rate of the 18:00 session open (later canon). Setup: price moves 0.1x the prior-day range away, then comes back to the open. Respected = +k trades before -k. Null = the same target distances and M1-bar horizon at matched random minutes. 50.6% against 49.9%: the 18:00 open behaves like a random price. Powered.

Same respect test with the midnight open (the earlier recording's reference). 48.7% against a 49.0% geometry-matched null. Neither open acts as support/resistance, and the 18:00-vs-midnight choice makes no difference. Powered.

Twitter-model gate on a 15m bare CISD book, restricted to events after the midnight open: shorts only above the midnight open, longs only below it (tested on the confirming close). Permitted trades come out -0.029R against the rest, on the wrong side of zero but not significant. Powered NULL. This is the one re-run: the first run (NULL, -0.022) admitted events decided exactly at 00:00, where the 'level' is the entry bar itself. The fix makes the open print strictly before the decision; the notes record this.

Deep premium/discount reading from b6yvRKf8haE and $niper: longs only below BOTH the midnight and 08:30 opens, shorts only above both. Same 15m CISD book, restricted to after 08:30. -0.036R, not significant and leaning negative. Powered NULL.

Futures 4H grid. When the 06:00 NY candle is a C2 reversal against the 02:00 candle, trade the 10:00 candle in the reversal direction: stop at the C2 extreme, 2R target, 4h hold. +0.079R against a matched random control; halves agree (H1 +0.118, H2 +0.043); powered (MDE 0.086). This is only a candidate: p=0.01 is unlikely to survive campaign Holm/BH, and the forex-grid version (b) is null. Exposure differs by 4.4% between the arms, under the 10% trigger, and ties are negligible.

Forex 4H grid (the grid the method spec locks for gold). A 05:00 C2 reversal against 01:00, then trade the 09:00 candle with the same stop, 2R target and 4h hold. +0.039R with a CI that includes 0. Powered NULL, just barely (MDE 0.096).

Three-tier filter plus the standing rules, on the 15m CISD book. Blocked: Monday sessions, NFP weeks before the 08:30 Friday release, and trades whose hold spans the release. Allowed arm: -0.010R. Powered NULL. NFP is the only calendar used; CPI and FOMC are unmodelled, which attenuates toward 0.

Earlier participation reading: trade only after 08:30 on red-folder days. Baseline is the 15m CISD events from 08:30 to 17:00 NY on Tue-Fri, and the gate is 'NFP day'. +0.027R, but there are only 123 NFP days (effective n below 200, MDE 0.14), so UNDERPOWERED.

Gate on the 5m bare CISD book: decision inside 10:00-11:00 NY, so every fill lands inside the window (entry by 10:55). +0.004R against the rest of the day. Powered NULL. The draw-on-liquidity precondition is not modelled; the concept only states the window.

Gate on the phase-3 15m CISD book (150min hold): decisions in his own-voice NY a.m. window 08:30-12:00 NY vs all other hours. -0.003R, CI [-0.033, +0.027]. The test was powered (MDE 0.043), so this is a NULL: the NY a.m.-only rule adds nothing on gold.

Stated policy ('nothing changes for me'). Gate on the 1h CISD book: trades on FOMC/NFP release days vs other days, claim '+'; a NULL would be consistent with this reading. -0.019R, CI [-0.12, +0.08], MDE 0.145 with about 204 release days, so it is UNDERPOWERED.

Observed deferral ('waiting for NFP'). Filter that blocks 1h CISD decisions made on a release day before the release (NFP 08:30, FOMC 14:00). +0.008R, CI [-0.13, +0.14]. The blocked arm is only about 192 days (MDE 0.195), so it is UNDERPOWERED.

'Ignore the calendar entirely.' The rule is the same as news-events-ignored reading a, so the test is the same too (same frame and settings, same hypothesis key): release-day vs other-day 1h CISD trades. -0.019R, CI [-0.12, +0.08], UNDERPOWERED.

'I don't trade post FOMC.' Filter that blocks 1h CISD decisions on FOMC days from 14:00 NY to the 18:00 roll. Only 47 blocked events on 39 effective days: +0.07R, CI [-0.19, +0.32], UNDERPOWERED. The '9:30 downgrade' clause is an expectation and was not tested.

Rate test on 30m candles, bias = prior-day candle direction, opposing-run and expansion cuts from threshold_fits at 1.0. Two branches pooled: an 8:30 opposing run predicts a 9:30 expansion; if 8:30 fails and 9:30 runs, it predicts a 10:00 expansion. The predicted slot expanded 32.3% of the time vs 33.4% for the same slot and direction on matched random days: -1.1pp, CI [-3.1, +1.0]. Powered NULL.

5m CISD book (50min hold), limited to events whose extreme bar traded through a prior 1D/4h/1h/1W/1M high or low. Gate: in-band POIs only (1D/4h/1h) vs events that tagged a weekly or monthly level. +0.018R, CI [-0.04, +0.07]. Powered (MDE 0.079), so a NULL: the out-of-band POIs he says to skip at a 5m entry do no worse.

Does the weekly step add value? Among 1h CISD trades already aligned with the prior-day candle, compare those also aligned with the prior-week candle against those that are not. Claim '+'; the concept predicts NULL. +0.011R, CI [-0.065, +0.085]. MDE is 0.107 against the 0.10 threshold, just UNDERPOWERED. The PWH/PWL = daily swing clause is an arithmetic identity and was not tested.

Magnet reading of 'fair value'. On each non-first trading day of a week, is the week's opening price (Sunday 18:00 NY) touched that day? It was touched 39.6% of the time vs 39.7% for a level at the same signed distance at matched random moments: -0.1pp, CI [-2.4, +2.0]. Powered NULL; the weekly open is no more of a magnet than any level at the same distance.

Faded the first 1H run of a mother-candle high or low when the prior days were all inside days and the run bar closed back inside. Stop at the run extreme, target the opposite external level, 24h trading-time hold. Only 146 trades with a very wide spread (tight stops, far targets, 21% win rate): MDE 1.35R, so underpowered. The halves disagree (H1 +1.45, H2 -0.29). News trigger not modelled.

Price engages PDH/PDL. Signal: an hourly close beyond the LOW (bullish: HIGH) of the last opposing candle that engaged it, confirmed 08:30-12:00 NY. Stop at the manipulation extreme, target the -2 SD projection, 10h hold. MDE 0.117 is just short of the 0.10 threshold, so underpowered. Rerun once with hold_basis=bars because real/control exposure differed by ~10% (trap 7). The first clock run gave +0.073 [-0.005,+0.151], also UNDERPOWERED.

Same as reading a, but the close must be beyond the candle's OPEN (its body). Underpowered (MDE 0.117). Rerun with hold_basis=bars for the trap-7 exposure gap (11%). The first clock run gave +0.053 [-0.029,+0.129]. Weekday/profile step and the 'convincing' qualifier were omitted.

Gate on the batch's 5m unicorn limit book (8,222 trades). Gated = unicorn in the direction of the latest daily C2, its sweep reached the C2's 50% EQ (the only T-spot construction in the corpus: 'just the equilibrium'), and no 1H close has passed the EQ, within 5 days. Only 38 gated trades, so underpowered. The TTFM indicator's T-spot derivation is withheld in the corpus, so only the EQ reading was tested.

Gate on the 5m unicorn limit book: breaker L1->H1->lower low->close through H1, with an overlapping same-direction FVG. Limit at the overlap edge, stop at the breaker's far edge, 2R, 50 min hold. Gated = formation count from L1 to completion <= 12 bars (3,462) vs 13-48 bars (4,758). The gate adds nothing: powered NULL, MDE 0.091.

15m sequence: a swing extreme inside the London (02-05) or NY (07-10) kill zone makes a fresh sweep of the Asia range, previous day or Monday high/low, then a CISD close within 3 bars in the same zone (entry 2, 'order block turned breaker'). Stop at the swept extreme, target the nearest of the Asia/Monday/PD opposite levels, 150 min hold. Only 193 trades, MDE 0.174, so underpowered. Not modelled: the balanced-price-range entry 1, the break-even move, daily bias and the H1 POI.

NickDoesFutures unicorn on 5m: the stop run takes the Asia range or previous-day extreme, and the unicorn completes 09:00-11:00 NY. Limit at the overlap edge rests until min(60 min, 11:00), cancelled if 2R trades first. Stop at the breaker's far edge; 2R is the 80% leg (the 3R remainder is not modelled). No daily bias. 360 trades, MDE 0.21, so underpowered.

Gate on the 5m breaker-retest book (27,065 filled): limit at the breaker's near edge, stop at its far edge, 2R, 50 min hold. Gated = wick-only breakers, meaning no 5m body closed beyond L1 during the lower-low leg (8,234), vs body-violated (18,823). Powered NULL (MDE 0.054). The point estimate is slightly against the claim and both halves are negative.

15m CISD by his definition (close past the first candle's open, POI gate on, 2/2 swing, max_wait 3), stop at the protected swing, 2R, 150min, against a matched control: -0.007R, a powered NULL (MDE 0.019).
Same book, but the close must clear the whole series' far extreme (the wording in hourly-cisd-confirmation): -0.008R, a powered NULL.

Gate on the cisd-a book: kept trades (>=1R of room between the closure and the short-term target, taken as the last confirmed opposite 2/2 swing before the extreme) vs skipped ones gave +0.008R, a powered NULL. The skip condition fired on 88% of CISDs.

Gate on 15m POI-on CISD closures allowed up to 40 bars late: fast (V-shaped, within 3 bars) closures vs slow ones (which the concept calls consolidation sweeps) gave -0.010R, a powered NULL. Slow closures are not measurably worse.

Continuation entry after a confirmed 15m CISD: a same-direction CISD off an FVG tag or swing sweep, with a higher low / lower high and the earlier protected swing intact, entered at market on the closure, stop at the new protected swing, 2R: -0.014R, a powered NULL.
4H/15m: CISDs taken after the 4H C2 closed (continuation in C3) vs early CISDs inside a still-forming 4H C2 gave +0.017R, a powered NULL (MDE 0.061).

1H close past the HIGH (bearish: LOW) of the opposing series that made the day's running extreme (18:00 NY day) confirms the daily wick; long/short with the stop at the day's extreme, 2R, 10h: +0.014R, a powered NULL.
Same book with the level at the first candle's open (the order-block wording): +0.016R, a powered NULL.

Intracandle CISD, rule as stated: a POI-backed 15m CISD aligned with the 4H continuation direction (previous-candle engine), extreme on the wick side of the 4H open, early only (first 2h of the candle), entry on the close, 2R: +0.009R, a powered NULL.
Timing rule as a gate over all IC-CISDs: early (<=2h into the 4H candle) vs late gave +0.021R, NULL (powered, MDE 0.081).
Bare 0.705 OTE limit on 15m close-through displacement legs (stop at the leg anchor, target the leg extreme, 5h hold) vs matched random entry: +0.001R, a powered null.
Gate on the OTE book: does a same-direction 15m FVG overlapping the 0.62-0.79 band help? -0.026R, CI contains 0. MDE 0.12 is above the 0.10 threshold, so underpowered.

Canonical 15m four-point breaker (H, L, HH, then a close below L1), first retest of the block's body edge, stop at the wick extreme, 2R: +0.042R vs control, both halves positive. EDGE candidate only (p=0.032, weak); it needs to survive Holm/BH.
Host's hard requirement of a higher-timeframe bias, tested as a gate on the breaker book: direction agrees with the daily previous-candle bias. -0.044R (wrong sign), CI contains 0, underpowered.

Confident variant: in a 15m swing trend, fade the raid of the last swing high or low at the first M1 through it, with a fixed stop of 0.5 x ATR(14), targeting the opposing swing. +0.012R, a powered null.
Conservative variant: the raiding 15m bar closes back inside, enter on that close, stop on the raid extreme, target the opposing swing. -0.05R with a wide CI (MDE 0.18), underpowered.

Union book at the same 1h FVGs, validated-order-block entries vs gap-limit entries. Limit arm: 2R, stop past the gap's far edge. Validated arm: 5m CISD inside the gap, entered on its close, 2R. Validated beat limit by +0.018R, a powered null. Limit bars that also traded through the far edge were dropped, which favours the limit arm.

Hourly half of the claim: the method-spec section 4.1 POI gate (detectors/poi.py, required at 1h, using bars up to the decision only) on the phase-3 rung-0 1h CISD book. POI-passing (80%) beat the rest by +0.096R, both halves positive (H1 +0.062, H2 +0.124). EDGE candidate; it needs Holm/BH.

15m/5m/1m ladder (M1 stands in for the 15s chart, which is not in the data). Union book of nested-gap entries vs the unrefined 15m-FVG-in-OTE entries at the same legs: +0.028R, CI contains 0, MDE 0.128, underpowered. Both arms enter at the next M1 open, which dilutes the difference.

1h C2 plus a 5m CISD inside C2; in C3, price trades into the T-spot and a 1m opposing FVG is closed through. Enter on that close, stop at the C3 wick, 2R, 5h hold. -0.007R, a powered null. The T-spot is a declared stand-in (the C2 half between its extreme and its EQ) because the author withholds the derivation.
Same entries, no target, exit at the C3 (1h) close: -0.000R, a powered null.

3-day stand-aside: 1h CISD entries in the direction of 3 consecutive daily closes beyond the prior day's extreme, vs all other 1h CISD trades, claim '-'. -0.021R with 228 gated trades (2.9%, effective n 125), underpowered.

End of the HTF expansion candle: 5m CISD entries taken when the in-progress 1h candle has already traded beyond the prior 1h extreme in the trade direction and 20 or more minutes have elapsed, vs other 5m CISD trades, claim '-'. -0.027R, CI [-0.043, -0.011], both halves negative, powered. EDGE candidate in the claimed direction; small effect, needs Holm/BH.

Order-type rule (market order rather than stop order). The harness entry is already a market fill at the next M1 open, and entry_mode is locked, so any book would test the trigger, not the order type. The stated measurables (slippage, mid vs market fills, platform lag, options) need fill or quote data that mid-price M1 OHLC does not have.

trade_test. Range: 8 x 30m candles spanning <=1.5 ATR. A 5m sweep of one extreme, landing inside an unmitigated same-direction 1H FVG, then a 5m CISD within 2h. Stop at the swept extreme, target the opposite range extreme. Result +0.155R vs control, CI contains 0, MDE 0.25 (n=370).

gate_test on the same 1H FVGs (>=0.25 ATR): the 0.5 (CE) entry vs the near-edge entry, same far-edge stop and same fixed target, clustered by gap. Result -0.029R control-adjusted, CI contains 0, MDE 0.18. Only refinement method 1 was tested; methods 2 and 3 have no bounds.

trade_test. A 15m swing pool is taken, then a 1m close through the short-term high/low with threshold_fits displacement (N=4, r1.5, d0.65), and a discount FVG in the leg. Limit entry at the FVG edge, stop at the leg extreme, 2R. Result +0.040R vs control, CI contains 0, powered NULL (MDE 0.070).

trade_test. News proxy: 08:30 NY 5m spike (>=3x median range) with a >=50% wick at the range extreme. The fib is anchored on the spike body (wick excluded), entry at the 0.5 of the adjusted range, stop at the wick, target the reversal extreme. Result +0.156R, CI contains 0, n=65 (no calendar in the data).

gate_test on 1H CISD setups with a fixed HTF target (2R). Gated arm: 5m CISD refinement (5m stop). Complement: direct 1H execution (1H stop). Clustered by setup. Result -0.034R, CI contains 0, MDE 0.104, just short of the 0.10 threshold.

gate_test on the same 5m entries. Stop at the genuine 1H invalidation (the protected swing) vs the default-timeframe 5m swing stop, same HTF target, clustered by setup. Result +0.003R, CI contains 0, MDE 0.103, just short of the 0.10 threshold.

trade_test. Side of the curve comes from 15m displacement breaks (threshold_fits). A 1m short-term low (or high) is taken by a candle that closes back inside, on the matching side. Stop at the swept extreme, 2R, 10min hold. Stop-first scoring gave EDGE +0.058R, but 50/50 tie scoring gave +0.021R UNDERPOWERED. Ambiguous-exit share: 9.6% real vs 12.1% control. Tie rule -> UNTESTABLE.

Claim is about depth-of-market (pulled vs filled level-2 size, displayed size vs traded delta), stated for ES. The data is XAUUSD OTC M1 OHLC only, with no book, no tape and no volume, so it cannot be tested.

Gate on the 5m bare-CISD baseline (98,346 trades, 2R, 50 min hold). Gate: the CISD extreme ran a 3-candle 5m swing (within 12 bars) into an unfilled 1H FVG (within 24h); it fired on 10.5%. Gated minus complement = +0.020R, CI [-0.003, +0.045]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.034).

Daily alternation rate test pooling both legs: a first FVG tag leads to the nearest unswept 3-candle swing, and a swing run leads to the nearest untagged FVG edge (20-session memory, 5-session horizon). Hit rate 25.7% vs geometry-matched null 26.7%. MDE 0.053 is just above the 0.05 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED.

Needs a DXY series and a Treasury yield or bond series, and the workspace has neither (only XAU M1 and XAG/EUR H1/D1). The claim is about DXY, not gold, and the source never says whether the bond chart is price or yield, which flips the sign of the divergence.

Baseline: first-tag reversal trades at a daily FVG, entered on the 4H forex grid (stop beyond the array, 2R, 40h hold in bar time); 439 trades. Gate: the prior day of 4H bars stopped within 0.5 daily ATR of the array and ranged at most 1 daily ATR; it fired on 27%. Diff +0.24R, CI [-0.02, +0.52], MDE 0.38, so UNDERPOWERED.

Reading a (SMT only at structural extremes): 1h CISD trades whose extreme took gold's PDH/PDL (1,840). Gate: XAG failed to take its own PDH/PDL by the confirm bar; it fired on 27%. Diff +0.05R, CI [-0.057, +0.161], MDE 0.156, so UNDERPOWERED.

Reading b (SMT at any scale, intra-range): all 8,034 1h CISD trades. Gate: 1h gold/XAG SMT at the nearest 2/2 swing within 20 bars of the extreme; it fired on 31%. Diff +0.000R, CI [-0.054, +0.054]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.077).

Daily inside-bar breakouts that closed beyond the inside bar, targeting the nearest untaken high/low among the 10 prior candles within 5 sessions. Hit rate 72.3% vs geometry-matched null 76.6%. Only 119 events and MDE 0.124, so UNDERPOWERED.

After a 1H CISD reversal: is the nearest untaken consolidation low (4 bars within 1 ATR, inside a 72-bar leg) reached within one session? Hit rate 47.9% vs geometry-matched null 49.3%. Powered NULL (MDE 0.035).
Needs traded volume on 15s/30s/1m futures bars. No XAU file has a volume or tick column or any sub-minute bars, and spot gold is OTC. Using M1 range as a stand-in would test a different concept.

Reading A (SMT confirms an existing model). Baseline: the phase-3 1h CISD book (protected-swing stop, 2R, 10h). Gate: a same-direction hourly gold/XAG SMT printed in the 3h up to the CISD close. The gate fires on 17% of trades; control-adjusted diff +0.013R, CI [-0.065, +0.092]. MDE 0.112 is above the 0.10 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED.

Reading B (trade the SMT directly). Takes the SMTs where silver swept and gold held, enters gold with the stop at gold's held low/high, 2R target, 10h. Diff vs the matched control is -0.013R, CI [-0.058, +0.034]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.066).

Bare hourly gold/XAG SMT at a shared 2/2 swing (lows bullish, highs bearish), traded in gold with a symmetric 1xATR14 stop, 1R target and 10h hold. Diff -0.007R, CI [-0.031, +0.019]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.035): the direction of the SMT does not predict the next move.
Same book as reading a, but only SMTs whose sweeping asset closes back beyond the swept level (a reversal closure). Diff -0.025R, CI [-0.056, +0.006]. Powered NULL, leaning negative.

Gold 1h. After external liquidity is taken (a sweep of an untaken 2/2 swing from the last 50 bars), the nearest untouched opposite-side FVG's near edge is reached within 600 M1 bars 49.1% of the time, against 47.3% for a same-distance null at random times. Diff +1.8pp, CI [+0.4, +3.2]pp, both halves positive: EDGE candidate. The effect is small (lift about 4%, well under the 5pp threshold). The null matches distance and side but not the post-sweep state, so this may be ordinary short-term retracement after a sweep rather than anything specific to the FVG. It needs Holm/BH survival and a post-sweep null before it is believed.

Same events as reading a, but the target is the FVG's consequent encroachment (midpoint): 44.4% vs a 42.8% null. Diff +1.5pp, CI [+0.1, +2.9]pp, halves agree: EDGE candidate.
