It is almost the same test as reading a, so it is not independent evidence, and it carries the same post-sweep-retracement caveat. p=0.027 is unlikely to survive campaign-wide Holm.

Claim '-': the level gold held in a silver-swept SMT should break less often than chance. It breaks within 600 M1 bars 61.1% of the time, against 59.7% for a same-distance null. Diff +1.4pp (the wrong sign), CI [-0.3, +3.2]pp. Powered NULL: the held level is no more respected than an arbitrary level at the same distance.

Gold and XAG both print a same-direction 1h FVG on the same bar. Within 20 bars exactly one of them trades into its gap's near edge, and gold is traded away from the gap (1xATR stop, 1R, 10h). Diff +0.030R, CI [-0.009, +0.065]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.053).

Baseline: every hourly SMT traded directly (1xATR stop, 1R, 10h), 7,136 events. Gate: a same-direction 1h CISD (the model) confirmed within the 3h before the SMT; it fires on 20%. Model-first minus SMT-first is +0.021R, CI [-0.048, +0.092]. MDE 0.1002 against the 0.10 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED by a hair. The point estimate has the claimed sign.

Bias-required reading (Ash Trades / $niper). Baseline: phase-3 rung-0 1h CISD book, n=8,030. Gate: trade direction matches the daily bias from the method-spec previous-candle engine on the last completed daily candle. Aligned arm n=3,564; the gate adds +0.040R, CI [-0.017, +0.097]. Powered, so NULL.

Bias-free reading (HolyAngelBruv / DTR): with no daily bias, trade structure breaks. Book: 1h CISD trades taken on no-bias days only. +0.033R vs the matched control, CI [-0.044, +0.118]. Effective n is 295 and MDE 0.116, so UNDERPOWERED.

Setup: a 1h C2 sweeps the previous hour's extreme into a POI (PDL/PWL, session levels, 1h swings, 1h FVGs). A 5m unicorn (breaker plus an overlapping FVG, within 12 candles) forms inside C2 and the trade is taken there. Stop at the C2 extreme, 2R, 4h hold. -0.044R vs control, CI [-0.132, +0.046]. MDE 0.128, so UNDERPOWERED.

Selection: no Mondays, no pre-NFP Thursdays, the prior day not an expansion, and the day is a remaining day of a confirmed weekly profile. Selected days print a large-range trending candle (range >= ADR20 and body >= half the range) 29.1% of the time vs a 24.0% regime-matched base rate: +5.2pp, CI [+0.6, +9.4]pp. The CI excludes 0 in the claimed direction, but MDE is 0.063 against the 0.05 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED. This is a candidate, not an EDGE. CPI/FOMC dates are not in the dataset, so step 1 is only partly applied.

Three weekly profiles (classic expansion, midweek reversal, consolidation reversal) are rebuilt from daily closes. Each remaining day is traded in the profile's direction at 09:30 NY. Stop at the week's extreme with a floor of 0.25 ADR, 2R, hold to 16:00 NY. +0.009R vs control, CI [-0.029, +0.047]. Powered, so NULL. Classic expansion supplies 904 of the 962 trades.

An expansion is 'anticipated' when daily order flow (daily closes against daily FVGs) is established and no consolidation trigger fires. The next day expands in that direction (body >= 0.5 ADR20) 21.5% of the time vs a 20.5% same-direction base rate within +/-30 days: +1.0pp, CI [-1.4, +3.4]pp. Powered, so NULL.

Event: any of the three triggers fires (first take of the prior week's high or low this week; overextension; close at the EQ of the dealing range). The next day is a consolidation day (|close-open| <= 0.2 ADR20) 28.5% of the time vs a 27.8% regime-matched base rate: +0.7pp, CI [-2.0, +3.3]pp. Powered, so NULL.

Event: daily order flow agrees with the nearer objective (an unmitigated daily swing high/low or a live daily FVG). The objective is reached within 5 sessions 69.0% of the time vs a 70.3% geometry-matched null (same distance, same side, same M1 horizon): -1.3pp, CI [-5.1, +2.1]pp. MDE 0.052 against the 0.05 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED.

Previous-candle engine on daily candles (18:00 NY). Trade D+1 toward D's bias-side extreme, stop at D's other extreme, hold one session in bars. Powered NULL, +0.027R. Re-run once: the first run's 30-minute time-of-day control match made 45% of control draws the concept's own trades, so it could only come out UNDERPOWERED. Noted in the result.
The same engine run candle by candle on 4H (forex grid), trading the next 4H candle toward the prior candle's bias-side extreme. Well-powered NULL, +0.004R.

Gate test of the conservative variant: take HTF-bias entries only after the opposite 1h swing liquidity is grabbed. Baseline is 1h closes the day after a daily C2/C3+H1-CISD bias. +0.14R [-0.0001,+0.29], MDE 0.21, UNDERPOWERED. H1 +0.36 and H2 -0.10 disagree. The clock-basis run had a 10.3% exposure gap, so it was re-run once with bars per README trap 7. That first run was also UNDERPOWERED because the halves disagreed.

Same-day reversal branch: a 1h CISD whose extreme swept PDH/PDL and is the day's running extreme, first one per day. Stop at the wick, target the opposite previous-day extreme, exit 17:00 NY. NULL, +0.056R, just powered (MDE 0.093).

Next-day bias: a daily C2 or C3 (C2-open reference) closure plus a same-direction H1 CISD gives 867 biased days, matching phase 3's 862. Traded the next session toward D's bias-side extreme with the stop at D's wick. NULL, -0.013R.

Gate: the profile confirms when the day formed its opposing extreme (opposing run > 0.30 of the running range) and price is now beyond the open in the bias direction. Baseline is 1h closes 03:00-12:00 NY on bias days. +0.105R, CI [-0.061,+0.256], effective n 226, UNDERPOWERED.

4H C2 (forex grid) confirmed by a same-direction 15m CISD inside C2. The POI is the C1 sweep itself. Traded C3 with the stop at the C2 extreme, target the nearest unswept C1/C2 far extreme, one 4H candle hold. +0.029R [+0.002,+0.056], halves agree (+0.017/+0.038), powered, so EDGE. This is only a candidate: p=0.037 will probably not survive campaign Holm/BH.
The same C2 model on the 1H/5m playbook pairing, one 1h candle hold. Well-powered NULL, +0.005R (MDE 0.027).
4H C3 closure, Reading A: the prior candle took the extreme without a C2 and this candle closes beyond C2's open. Traded C4 at 2R with the stop at the C2/C3 swing, one 4H candle hold. NULL, +0.022R.
4H C3 closure, Reading B: the close must clear C2's extreme, a strict subset of Reading A. Same trade. NULL, +0.019R.

External to internal leg on 1h: sweep of an untaken 2/2 swing that closes back inside (failed displacement). Target the near edge of the nearest unmitigated opposite FVG, stop at the sweep wick, 10h hold. +0.041R, MDE 0.124, UNDERPOWERED.

Internal to external leg on 1h: price tags an unmitigated FVG and closes back out of it (respected). Stop at the FVG's far edge, target the nearest untaken swing beyond, 10h hold. +0.069R [-0.006,+0.146], MDE 0.109, UNDERPOWERED.

A valid daily C2/C3+H1 CISD model fails at the first 1h close beyond D's EQ on D+1. Traded the opposite way at that close, stop at the session's running extreme, target D's opposite extreme. +0.034R, n=427, UNDERPOWERED. Re-run once with hold_basis=bars because the clock run's exposure gap was over 10%. The clock run was also UNDERPOWERED.

Same EQ invalidation, but the entry waits for a 1h CISD in the new direction; stop at its protected swing, target D's opposite extreme. -0.024R, n=322, UNDERPOWERED. Re-run once with bars hold basis per trap 7 (the clock run was also UNDERPOWERED).
Daily C2 at the week-to-date extreme, confirmed by a 1h CISD at the daily wick, traded the next session (stop at the extreme, 2R). +0.026R vs control, CI [-0.054,+0.111], MDE 0.118. Underpowered.
Gate test: does the hourly CISD confirmation improve week-extreme daily C2 candle-3 trades (898 total, 543 gated)? +0.011R, CI [-0.147,+0.158]. Underpowered.

15m CISD book (28,302 events): continuation CISDs (higher low / lower high after a same-direction CISD whose swing held) vs reversal CISDs. -0.004R, CI [-0.032,+0.023], MDE 0.040. Powered null: continuations are no better than reversals.
London ran through the midnight open but did not reach PDL/PDH; a 5m CISD in NY 08:30-12:00 off an extreme beyond PDL/PDH; 2R, flat at 17:00. +0.094R, CI [-0.033,+0.210], MDE 0.174. Underpowered.

Describes the settings of a TradingView indicator and makes no market claim. The C2/C3/C4 print rules it encodes are paywalled (CqMIh-Vvhbg), and both stated measurables need the proprietary indicator's own output.

With a PD array: London 02-05 made the day's extreme beyond PDL/PDH plus a 15m CISD; entry on the first same-direction NY 5m CISD with the London extreme intact; 2R. n=132, +0.174R, CI [-0.073,+0.425]. Underpowered.
Shape-only reading, no PD array required: London extreme plus a 15m CISD, then a NY 5m continuation CISD; 2R. +0.018R, CI [-0.127,+0.161]. Underpowered.

Day took PDL/PDH; a 1h CISD off the day's extreme with price still beyond the 18:00 open; target the daily open, flat at 17:00. +0.002R, CI [-0.057,+0.060], MDE 0.083. Powered null: the open is no magnet.
Same entries, target = the day's opposing extreme so far (the variant). +0.006R, CI [-0.064,+0.072], MDE 0.097. Powered null.

Tier 1 (C3 after a large-wick daily C2, 1h CISD holding 0.5 of the wick, 2R) vs tier 3 (the day's own reversal candle traded to the daily open); 892 events, 448 tier 1. +0.045R, CI [-0.094,+0.181]. Underpowered. Tier 2 cannot be separated live.

Daily C2 bias, a same-direction 4h C2 (forex grid), then the first 15m CISD inside 4h C3 holding the C2 half; 2R, 150 min. -0.022R, CI [-0.169,+0.128]. Underpowered, and the sign agrees with phase 3's -0.028R.
London stayed inside the prior day's range; a 5m CISD off an 08:30-10:00 sweep of the London high/low; target PDH/PDL, flat at 17:00. +0.024R, CI [-0.085,+0.134], MDE 0.157. Underpowered.

TradingView workspace and display configuration. It makes no claim about price, and the only data-relevant settings (NY time with DST, full session, continuous contract) are already fixed in the harness.

Uses the concept's own ladder: 1H draw, 15m opposite stop raid with close back in, entry on the first 1m FVG retrace, stop at the raid extreme, 1:1. Beats the matched control by +0.027R. This is only a candidate: H1 +0.055, H2 +0.004, and net avg_R is still -0.024. It needs Holm/BH survival.
The pattern alone on 5m (breaker plus overlapping FVG, limit at the overlap edge, stop at the swept extreme, 2R). A powered zero against the matched control.
The same unicorn restricted to setups confirmed at a session open (London 02:00-05:00, NY 09:30-11:00). A powered zero.
Autobias 1: 5m CISD setups that agree with the last 4H (forex grid) C2 closure direction, compared with the setups it suppresses. A powered zero.
Autobias 2: the same book gated on agreement with the last daily C2 closure direction. A powered zero.

On no-bias days (prior daily candle neither C2 nor C3), the nearer 18:00-09:30 range extreme is taken first 60.7% of the time vs a 60.0% geometry-matched null at the same clock. Nearness explains it all.
The rotation claim, that both pre-open extremes are taken 09:30-16:00 on no-bias days: 5.9% vs 8.2% for the matched null. Rotation is rarer than chance, the opposite of what the concept claims.

The guests' dollar-first gate applied to gold: 1h CISD trades that oppose the dollar, read from the last completed EURUSD weekly candle inverted as a DXY proxy, compared with vetoed trades. Powered NULL, with the point estimate negative.
The FX pair-selection procedure (rank currency futures, trade crosses while the dollar consolidates) needs DXY, currency futures and FX crosses, and the campaign trades only XAUUSD.

The four-candle window read as a hard window: 5m CISD entries in the direction of the last 1H C2, taken during C3/C4 vs C5/C6. Entries inside the window are not better (powered NULL, point estimate negative).
The C1-C4 numbering convention and the indicator's four-candle display default are labelling definitions that assert nothing about price.
Model 1 on 1m in the 08:30-11:00 NY open: liquidity grab, then BOS close with an FVG, retrace into the FVG, stop at the grab extreme, 2R. A powered zero.
Model 3 vs model 1: requiring the FVG entry to sit in the 0.62-0.79 OTE of the displacement leg. It passes only 11.9% of setups. The MDE of 0.115 exceeds 0.10, so the result is underpowered.

A plan for running many prop accounts (trailing drawdown, payout schedules, account count). Nothing to test in XAU OHLC: the aggressive phase has no entry, stop or size, and the '100 ticks / close once profitable enough' exit has no entry model and no defined threshold.

Gate on the phase-3 5m CISD book (2R, 50 min): keep trades whose target distance is at most 1.3x the ADR the day has left (126-day ADR). Gated 71k trades vs 22k complement: -0.005R [-0.022, +0.011]. Powered NULL.

'Beyond the ADR means reversal': fade the extension at the first M1 close each day where the day's range reaches the ADR (stop 0.25 ADR, 1R, 4h, control matched on time of day). Result +0.020R [-0.038, +0.080] vs matched random entries. Powered NULL.

The add itself: a same-direction 30m STRAT 2-2 trigger inside the 30m bar where a winning 15m 2-2 (with 1D+1h continuity) hit its magnitude target. 30m stop and magnitude target, 5h hold. Result -0.007R [-0.034, +0.021] vs matched control. Powered NULL. Only the 15m-to-30m rung was tested.

15m STRAT 2-2 trades with continuity. At each 15m close while a trade is alive (up to 16 bars), score 'keep holding' (original stop, no target, 1h), clustered by trade. Holding after a close with no opposing 2 (69k rows) vs holding after the opposing-2 close (16k rows): -0.018R [-0.050, +0.012]. Powered NULL; ctrl_overlap 0.175.

Ben's reading (move to break-even or to the second tranche's stop on adding) depends on an add whose trigger and tranche ratio are never stated. Picking an add rule would test our model, not his. The harness also scores one fixed stop per trade.
NickDoesFutures variant (an add must never raise open risk above the initial risk) is a risk-accounting rule with no price claim, and it does not say where the stop moves to.
Arithmetic reductio with no market claim. Checked: 1%/day gives x10 at 231.4 days, x100 at 462.8, x1000 at 694.2, x10k at 925.6 and x100k at 1157. That matches the quoted ladder from a $1,000 start.

Gate on the rung-0 1h CISD book: take at most 3 trades per week and stop after 2 known winners. Taken 1,637 vs 6,358 later-in-week trades: -0.038R [-0.103, +0.031]. NULL, just powered (MDE 0.096). The A+ selection mechanism itself cannot be reproduced mechanically.

A combinatorial claim about losing-streak length plus sizing advice, with no price claim. For context, the expected longest losing run in 1,000 i.i.d. trades is about 9 at a 50% win rate, 7 at 60% and 16 at 30%. So '5-10 in a row' holds for win rates of roughly 45-70%.

Only the checklist items decidable from OHLC: Monday, or London took both Asia extremes. Gate on the 5m CISD book in NY AM 08:30-12:00, claim '-'. Flagged 4,275 vs 10,519 unflagged: -0.036R [-0.074, +0.003], p=0.068. Powered NULL, leaning in the claimed direction. Items needing an economic calendar and the undefined ones were not tested.

First trading session of the month (quarter starts included) as a 'manipulation-heavy' flag on the same NY AM 5m CISD book, claim '-'. Flagged 706 trades: +0.028R [-0.055, +0.110]. UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.117, effective n 126).

Tested 2R as a floor. The book was 1h CISD entries targeting the prior day's high or low; the gate kept setups where that target was at least 2R away (33% of 6,065). Floor-passing setups did no better than the rest (-0.040R, CI [-0.114, +0.030]). The test was just short of power (MDE 0.1025).

Compared a fixed 2R target with a fixed 1R target on the same 1h CISD entries. Each arm was adjusted by its own matched control. The difference was +0.002R, CI [-0.031, +0.034]: a powered null (MDE 0.046). The script was run twice because the first write was refused on a params_source prefix; the test is deterministic, so both runs share one hyp_key.

The harness cannot move a stop mid-trade, so the trail was tested as the position it leaves. That position starts at the first later same-direction 1h CISD while the base trade (prior-day target at least 2R away) is still open. Its stop is the new protected swing, capped at 50% of the day's running range, and its target is the original one. It was no better than random entries with the same geometry (-0.016R, CI [-0.109, +0.077]). Only 454 events.

Book: 15m CISD at 2R, 150-minute hold. The gate kept the first signal of each trading day (day rolls at 18:00 NY) against the later signals the cap would skip. First signals were no different (-0.017R, CI [-0.066, +0.031]): a powered null. The tilt and psychology justification is not decidable from price data.

Untestable: this is pure sizing arithmetic. Position size changes dollars, never a trade's R outcome, and the concept claims no market effect in either direction to test. The 34% break-even at 2R is the identity 1/(1+2).

Reading A (TTrades): half the position exits at 2R and half runs to the prior day's high or low, compared with one full exit at that level. Entries: 1h CISD where that level is at least 2R away. The difference was +0.005R, CI [-0.076, +0.087], underpowered. The trailed runner cannot be modelled; the runner keeps the original stop. The gated n counts legs, so it is about 2 x 1,992 entries.
Reading B (the guest): no intraday partials, one full exit at the draw, claim '+'. This is the same comparison as reading a with the opposite claim: -0.005R, CI [-0.094, +0.078], underpowered.

The benchmark 4H/15m model at a fixed 2R with no management. Entries: 15m CISD in the direction of the 4H previous-candle bias (forex grid). It did not beat matched random entries (+0.006R, CI [-0.016, +0.029]): a powered null. Raw win rate was 42%, against the claimed 63% (recorded in notes only; not a verdict input).

Mechanical re-run of the silver-bullet AM model on gold. A sweep of the 09:00 NY hourly range during 10:00-11:00 NY, then a 1m CISD in the other direction. Stop at the swept extreme, target the far side of the range, 5h hold. Median planned RR was 3.8. The book did not beat random entries (-0.034R, CI [-0.127, +0.059]), underpowered. Break-even at 3R was not applied (not expressible).

Stop at the protected-swing wick versus the body extreme of the opposing series, on the same 1h CISD entries at 2R. The wick stop was not better (-0.009R, CI [-0.048, +0.027]): a powered null. Only one reading was run, the channel's canonical wick vs body contrast.

Reading A: a limit at the order block's mean threshold (live 3h, cancelled if the 2R objective trades first), same structural stop, 2R. Compared with a market entry on the same 1h CISD. There was no difference (+0.005R, CI [-0.053, +0.067]): a powered null. The limit is approximated by entering at the next M1 open after the touch. 22 fills whose own bar also hit the stop could not be scored, which slightly flatters this arm.
Reading B (keep the stop, cut position size) is untestable: it is sizing arithmetic. It changes dollars per trade, not R, so it is identical to the baseline in any R-based test.
Procedure for rolling ES/NQ quarterly contracts by open interest and volume. It makes no claim about price, and XAUUSD spot has no contracts or OI/volume curve.
Ticks, handles and multipliers are units and sizing arithmetic with no market hypothesis. Multipliers cancel in R.
Frame the setup on NQ and execute an at-the-money QQQ option. Testing it needs option chain prices and an ETF; the campaign has only gold M1 OHLC.
Vehicle-choice argument (spread, slippage, PDT rule, tax). It needs fills or bid/ask from both venues, and cost cancels in the matched-control differential anyway.
Expiry-selection rule against theta decay. It needs option premia or implied vol, which the campaign lacks, and the corpus gives no method for estimating time-to-target.

At 2h into each forex-grid 4H candle whose running candle has a small wick (opp/body<=1.0), trade its direction with stop at the running extreme and hold to the 4H close (clock-matched control). The CI contains 0 (MDE 0.036), but 33% of control draws overlap real trades, so NULL is downgraded to UNDERPOWERED.
Book: 1h CISD aimed at the expansion target (PDH/PDL). Gate: the running daily candle has a large opposing run (>1.0 x body), claim '-'. Large-wick trades are not worse (powered NULL, MDE 0.088).
1h CISD on large-wick days with price still on the wick side of the 18:00 daily open, targeting that open. It does not beat a matched random entry (powered NULL).
5m relatively-equal highs/lows (within 0.10 ATR, 48 bars) are reached within 240 M1 bars 77.7% of the time vs 77.1% for an ATR-scaled distance-matched null. Powered NULL.

The near edge of a 15m FVG is revisited within 240 M1 bars 82.7% of the time vs 80.9% for an ATR-scaled distance-matched null, +1.8pp, with both halves positive. Candidate only: the event fires right after a displacement bar, so the edge may come from short-term reversal or volatility clustering rather than the gap. The near edge is the 3rd bar's own low/high, and the null matches distance in ATR units, not local post-displacement volatility.

Book: 15m CISD (2R, 150min). Gate: an unfilled 4H FVG or PDH/PDL marked at the 18:00 open was tagged earlier that day. Gated trades do worse (-0.034R); H1 carries it (H1 -0.058, H2 -0.012). Caveat: the gate correlates with time of day because tags come later in the day, and the control was not held to the NY clock (ctrl_tod_tol_min not set).
Book: bias-aligned 5m CISD, with bias = the previous day's candle direction. Gate: one of the two nearest aligned 1H FVG / PDH-PDL POIs was tagged earlier that day. Powered NULL (MDE 0.033).

Scored at the stop move (same design as the earlier no-stop-change and t1-t2 tests): 1h CISD trade, a 2m close over the prior 2m swing high, then the first 2m higher low becomes the stop, keeping the original 2R target and the rest of the 10h. The trailed leg vs random geometry: tight stops give a 11% win rate and high R variance. MDE 0.20 > 0.10, UNDERPOWERED.

Tested the claim that a filled 15m FVG is a better entry when price comes back to it (trading the filling leg's direction, stop beyond the band, 2R) than the first touch of an untouched FVG. Clustered by gap. Powered NULL: BPR revisits are no better. The untouched-gap arm itself beat its own control by +0.033R.

Used 15m 2/2 swing levels that were first pierced by a wick only. Compared AP's break entry (a body close beyond the wick extreme) with a body close beyond the level alone (setups where the two coincide were dropped; stop at the breaking bar's far extreme, 2R, 150min). Powered NULL, with the point estimate against the claim. Mean-R cannot see the trades AP's rule avoids.

Tested the claim that expansion never follows expansion. Expansion day = range at least 1.5x a trailing mean that skips the prior day, and opposing run/body at most 1. Measured how often the next day is a same-direction expansion versus a ±21-day random-day null, with claim '-'. The rate was 11.4% vs a null of 7.9%, the opposite direction to the claim (p=0.08). UNDERPOWERED: MDE 0.057 vs a threshold of 0.0196.

Large daily wick = wick bigger than the body and the other wick. On the next day, entered at the first H1 FVG inside the wick's near half (no H1 close beyond the wick EQ first). Stop at the wick EQ, target the wick day's opposite extreme, 10h hold. Diff was +0.117R, but the test is UNDERPOWERED (n=174, MDE 0.246); both halves were positive.

UNTESTABLE because the fib anchors and orientation cannot be recovered: the settings were shown on screen but never read out, so the 0.75 zone cannot be placed. The entry also depends on four objects this concept does not define (smart-money-reversal area, original consolidation, Silver Bullet below 0.50, mitigation block). The one mechanical rule left (a return to 0.50 invalidates) is a geometric identity, not a prediction.

Book of 30m breaks (first close beyond a 2/2 swing, stop at the extreme since the swing, 2R, 300min). Gate = the break takes an intermediate-term swing, i.e. a swing that formed inside an FVG from the prior 20 bars (AM Trades' MSB). Powered NULL, which supports the host's 'all the same' reading. One test settles both readings, so there is no reading b.

On 15m swing breaks, compared a limit return to the breaking candle (AP's BOS order block) with a return to the last opposing candle of the same break. Entry at the near body edge, stop at the far wick, 2R, 150min, clustered by break. Powered NULL, leaning against the claim (the CI upper bound is +0.0008).

Reversal branch on 15m: an expansion followed within 24 bars by an opposite expansion, traded that way (stop at E1's extreme, target E1's origin). +0.017R vs control, CI includes 0, MDE 0.124. Half the events were dropped because the origin was already taken at entry.
Bias alignment: 15m rung-0 CISD traded with vs against the direction of the latest 1h expansion. +0.025R, powered NULL.
1h expansion met by an opposite expansion: the rate at which E1's origin is taken within 1,440 M1 bars was 52.9%, against 54.5% for a null at the same distance and horizon. Diff -1.6pp, MDE 6.6pp.
Degraded-sequence filter (claim '-'): aligned 15m CISD continuations where the last three 1h expansions alternate direction. -0.013R vs the rest, powered NULL.
Continuation inside a live 1h expansion: a shallow pullback (<=0.5) into a 15m FVG, then a 15m CISD; stop at the protected swing, target the leg's unswept extreme. +0.020R, MDE 0.104.
Stand-aside after 3 expansion days (claim '-'): aligned 15m CISD continuations after three small-wick trading days in the trade direction. -0.006R, effective n 177.
SLOW reading: a shallow retracement that takes at least as long as the 1h expansion leg, then a 15m CISD continuation (stop L, target H). -0.078R, on the wrong side of the claim, MDE 0.118.
QUICK reading: a shallow retracement shorter than the expansion leg, then a 15m CISD continuation. +0.019R, powered NULL (MDE 0.079).

Daily reversal-wick candle built from 5m expansion met with expansion. Next-day first touch of 0.5 of low->close, stop at the wick extreme, target the candle's opposite extreme. +0.017R, MDE 0.195. Re-run once after a spec fix: the legs were first built on 1h, outside the concept's 5m/1m ltf list.
Same setup as reading a with the entry at 0.5 of the wick itself (half-wick-respect). -0.004R, MDE 0.223. Same single re-run after the ltf spec fix.
1h protected swing: a strict POI (a prior swing swept or an FVG reached, no fallback), then a close through the series' OPEN within 3 bars. Stop on the swing, 2R. -0.009R, powered NULL.
Same as reading a, but the close must go through the series' far EXTREME. -0.002R, powered NULL.

Failure branch: a 1h expansion into the prior day's low/high with no opposite expansion within 4 bars, traded as a continuation (stop at the retracement extreme, 2R). +0.129R with a CI excluding 0 in the claimed direction, but MDE 0.110 > 0.10, so the harness labels it UNDERPOWERED. H1 +0.17, H2 +0.07 (H2 CI includes 0). A candidate to watch, not an edge.
Qualification rule: 15m CISD whose opposing-series candles all have a wick on the extreme side, vs series containing a wickless candle (1,872 in the complement). +0.044R, powered NULL.

Rolling invalidation: inside a live 1h expansion, enter with the trend at each qualifying opposing 1h candle close. Stop beyond the series extreme, target the leg extreme. +0.039R; effective n 2,274 with heavy dependence and 12.7% control overlap, MDE 0.181.

5m: an ITH (a strict 3-bar STH with a lower STH on both sides) traded away from once the right-hand STH confirms, stop at the ITH, 2R, 50 min. +0.0096R vs the matched control, halves agree, powered. A tiny candidate EDGE that still needs Holm/BH.
Same book as reading a, but the ITH bar must sweep the prior STH (trade above it, then close back below it), as in the narrated chart procedure. Powered NULL (+0.008R).

15m proximity reading: two consecutive same-side 3-bar swings within 0.25 ATR14 of each other, the cluster's outer extreme treated as a target. Taken within 300 M1 bars 73.3% of the time vs a 73.7% distance-matched null. Powered NULL.

15m sweep reading: a lower swing high that failed to take the prior swing (mirror for lows). Revisited and taken within 300 M1 bars 75.7% of the time vs a 74.8% distance-matched null (+0.9pp), halves agree. A small candidate EDGE.

15m propulsion block: OB1 = phase-3 CISD series, then a retrace into OB1, then OB2 closed over. The opening-price limit is modelled as the next M1 open after the first touch, stop at the block low, 2R, 150 min. +0.035R vs control, halves agree, powered. Candidate EDGE; the limit-fill emulation is a caveat.

Same propulsion-block book with the stop on the block's body (lowest open/close) instead of its low. +0.046R vs control, halves agree, powered. Candidate EDGE with the same limit-fill caveat as reading a.
Gate on the 15m bare CISD: does the strict trigger also clear the whole-move level (the 'ignore small candles, take the whole move' reading)? The gate passed on 87% of triggers. Powered NULL.
Gate on the 15m bare CISD: does the first candle of the opposing series form a strict 3-bar swing (the 'skip a non-swing candle' reading)? Powered NULL.

1h: every strict 3-bar swing traded as a reversal at its confirmation, stop at the swing extreme, 2R, 10h. diff about 0. Labelled UNDERPOWERED rather than NULL because 23% of control draws overlap the concept's own trades (the r2 attenuation rule).
1h: only 'genuine' swings, i.e. those that take out the last confirmed same-side swing, traded as reversals. Powered NULL (+0.017R).

15m closes through a 2/2 STH/STL, entered at the open after the 4-candle window, stop at the 50% retracement of the leg, 1R. Gate = aggressive by the threshold_fits magnitude test (1.5/0.65), which passed on 41% of breaks. Aggressive breaks do not retrace less. Powered NULL.

Gold 1h CISD, kept when the strength order fits (short gold only when it is weaker than silver since the 18:00 NY open, long only when stronger). Gate = silver swept its 20-bar extreme and closed back inside within the last 3h. Only 395 gated trades (MDE 0.17): UNDERPOWERED.

Same strength-filtered gold 1h CISD book. Gate = a silver 1h CISD in the trade direction within the last 4h. The point estimate is against the claim (-0.065R) but the test is UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.115).
5m bare CISD on days whose prior daily candle was a C2/C3 closure. Gate = the CISD agrees with that daily closure's direction. Powered NULL (+0.001R).

5m bare CISD whose close sits inside an opposing, still-open 1h FVG (the 'retracement into an HTF PD array' reading), claim '-'. Point estimate -0.023R, in the claimed direction, but the CI includes 0. Powered NULL.

5m book that trades the first close through a 3-candle short-term swing (formed within 3 1h candles), gated on the broken swing being a type-1 intermediate-term swing (higher short-term lows on both sides). Gate fires on 17%. Powered zero.
Same 5m swing-break book, gated on the broken swing being 'rebalanced': its extreme printed inside an FVG that price reached for the first time. Gate fires on 9.5%. Powered zero.

1h CISD reversals off an internal extreme that has an untaken outer same-side swing in the 3-day window. Gate: separation from that outer swing >= 0.5 ADR (declared). Gate fires on only 8.6% (median separation 0.11 ADR), so the gated arm is too small: MDE 0.17.

Gold 1h CISD book gated on gold being the right asset against silver by tool 3 (closure): the confirming candle's body in own-ATR units beats silver's for a long, trails it for a short. Gate fires on 58%. Powered zero.
Same book, gated by tool 2 (separation): gold travelled further than silver from the shared reversal bar, in own-ATR units, in the trade direction. Gate fires on 62%. Powered, CI contains 0.

1h CISD reversals that swept an untaken 1h swing from the last 20 trading days, gated on at least one swept swing lying inside the 3-daily-candle window. Gate fires on 97.9%, so the complement has an effective n of 64. My design made the out-of-window arm too small: a sweep of an old swing almost always also sweeps a recent one.

Book that fades the first touch of every 1h 3-candle swing inside its 3-day window (stop 0.5 ATR1h beyond, 2R, 10h), gated on the swing being relevant: no untaken outer same-side swing within 0.5 ADR. Gate fires on 21% of 23,840 touches. Powered zero.

After gold has already taken its PDH/PDL, silver's first tag of its own PDH/PDL. Trading gold against the move (1 ATR stop, 1R) does worse than the matched control: gold continues rather than turns. The CI upper end sits at -0.002 and p=0.04, so this will not survive Holm.
Silver tags its PDH/PDL while gold has not taken its own (SMT at the level), then gold is traded against the move. Powered, CI contains 0, point estimate negative.
1m CISD book (the 15/5/1 execution TF, 10 min hold) gated on the 5m state (direction of the most recent closed 5m CISD) agreeing with the entry. Gate fires on 50%. Powered zero.

Same 1m book, gated on the full domino (5m and 15m states both agree). Gate fires on 31%. The effect is -0.009R: significant only because n is huge, far below the 0.10R threshold and unlikely to survive Holm. Either way, confirmation does not help.

The device transferred to XAU/XAG because ES and NQ are not in the data. Gold 1h CISD book gated on the prior completed day's ratio candle closing in the trade direction. Gate fires on 50%. Powered zero. This does not test the ES/NQ claim itself.
Bare 15m CISD (phase-3 config) inside the four forex kill zones. Entries after the first 30 minutes (n=15,034) vs entries at the start (n=3,163): +0.021R [-0.026, +0.063]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.063).
Does the 07:00-07:30 NY move go the opposite way to the 07:30-17:00 move? It did 49.5% of the time, against 51.0% for random 30-minute moves with the same bar counts. Powered NULL.
Bare 5m CISD. Setups from 04:00 to 17:00 NY vs setups from 18:00 to 04:00: -0.005R [-0.020, +0.010]. Powered NULL. Discarding pre-04:00 setups gains nothing.

Daily 09:30 fade: fade the 09:30-09:45 leg, stop at the leg's extreme, 2R, exit 16:00. No-news days (n=1,685) vs news days (n=972): +0.020R [-0.10, +0.14]. News days are derived NFP Fridays plus an 08:30 5m range at least 3x its 24h median; there is no calendar data. MDE 0.17, so UNDERPOWERED.
Ash's reading. Bare 5m CISD taken within 60 minutes of 02:00 or 09:30 NY vs all other times: -0.002R [-0.027, +0.023]. Powered NULL.
$niper and AM Trades' reading. Bare 5m CISD taken 09:30-12:00 NY vs all other times: +0.008R [-0.013, +0.029]. Powered NULL.

7h candles anchored at 18:00, so London is 01:00-08:00. After a London C2 reversal, New York (08:00-15:00) held the London candle's 50% level (or 50% of its wick when the wick is large) with no M1 close through it on 28.7% of days. The null, same distance at a similar NY time, held on 26.9%. Powered NULL (MDE 0.047 vs 0.05).

The C2-unicorn setup pooled over the three stated pairings (15m/1m, 1h/5m, 4h/15m) vs the matched control: -0.019R [-0.059, +0.022]. Powered NULL. Point estimates by pairing: 15m/1m -0.024, 1h/5m -0.065, 4h/15m +0.091 (n=398). Nothing supports it working at every scale.

Tag of the previous HTF bar's high or low, confirmed by a CISD on the LTF. Stop at the extreme, target at the opposite HTF extreme. $niper's paired LTF (1D->1h, 4h->15m, 1h->5m) vs one rung higher or lower: -0.006R [-0.023, +0.011], clustered by level. Powered NULL. The paired timeframe adds nothing.
Gate test: only taking entries in 08:30-11:00 NY (0bH_kkG2q6s) on the 5m bare-CISD book (98,346 events, 2R, 50 min). Gated minus complement is +0.005R [-0.017,+0.027]. A powered NULL (MDE 0.032).
Gate test: the 09:30-10:00 NY 'opening drive' window (G1IIdQ3RAkY) on the same 5m CISD book. +0.008R [-0.040,+0.059]. A powered NULL (MDE 0.071).

Gate test of the indicator's session filter. The concept's own video gives no bounds, so it uses the same indicator's stated 8-11 EST setting from Je7cd9HJUBE, read on the New York clock with DST. Run on the 5m CISD book: +0.005R [-0.017,+0.027]. A powered NULL. The time-zone part itself is tested under est-timezone-anchor.

Rate test: do the day's high and low (18:00 roll, 2,718 days) form inside London 02-05 or NY a.m. 08:30-12? Null: the same two windows shifted together to a random place in the day. Observed 37.4% vs null 25.3% (+12.1pp [+10.5,+13.7]), both halves agree. An EDGE candidate, but it is about when levels form (opportunity), not about entry accuracy.

Rate test: is 08:30 on the America/New_York clock (DST-aware) a volatility step? Measured as M1 range in the 15 min after it exceeding the 15 min before, against matched random :30 marks. 65.9% vs 55.6% (+10.1pp [+8.0,+12.9]). An EDGE candidate for the clock being a real event marker.

Same test with a literal fixed UTC-5 'EST' clock (08:30 EST = 13:30 UTC all year): 79.9% vs 55.4% (+24.4pp). This does NOT show that fixed EST is the right clock. In summer its 08:30 lands on the 09:30 NY cash open, which is a bigger volatility step. The DST question stays settled for America/New_York (session_window_fit).

Trade test of a Judas swing / order block at the 00:00 and 08:30 NY opens (09:30 dropped for forex, as the concept says). Rule: a 5m close back over the opposing-run candle within 60 min; stop at the run extreme, 2R, 50 min. avg_R -0.045, vs matched control -0.009R [-0.046,+0.026]. A powered NULL.

Gate test of the premium/discount rule: shorts above both the midnight and 08:30 opens, or longs below both. Run on 5m CISD entries in 08:35-17:00 NY (34,354 in the book, 9,695 gated). +0.003R [-0.024,+0.031]. A powered NULL.

Gate test: entries inside any forex kill zone (Asia 20-00, London 02-05, NY AM 07-10, London Close 10-12 NY) vs outside all of them, on the 5m CISD book. +0.007R [-0.007,+0.022]. A powered NULL (MDE 0.021).
Gate test of his own NY-open choice, 08:30-09:30 NY (CAuN4tvLInQ / A8UpRZlRzlg), on the 5m CISD book. +0.003R [-0.032,+0.036]. A powered NULL. The halves have opposite signs (H1 -0.045, H2 +0.045).

Pooled phase-3 5m and 15m CISD books. Gated = 5m in high volatility plus 15m in low volatility (recent/typical 5m range ratio above or below 1, declared before run). Result: no difference, powered NULL (MDE 0.018).
Alignment reading: a 5m CISD is gated when its direction matches the latest 1h CISD. Result +0.013R, CI contains 0, powered NULL (MDE 0.023).
HTF-level reading: a 5m CISD is gated only after price has traded through the prior 1h bar's low or high within the last 60 min. Result: powered NULL.

Kill-zone chain (prior NY AM, Asia, London, NY AM); manipulation = sweep of the prior window closing back inside. 15m CISD events in the predicted expansion session vs other sessions, with the control matched to NY clock time (ctrl_tod_tol_min=30). Result -0.026R, powered NULL (MDE 0.077).

Never trade after FOMC: 15m CISD decisions from 14:00 NY to the session end on scheduled FOMC days are blocked (125 events on 76 days). Structurally underpowered: effective n is 76 and MDE 0.30. The 'only three releases' preference has no outcome of its own and is not scored.

NFP-week day map on the 15m CISD book, NFP weeks only. Allowed = Tue/Wed, release day after 08:30, and any day after the release. Blocked = Mon, the day before the release, and release day before 08:30. Result -0.040R, powered NULL (MDE 0.075).

Friday fade of the NFP sweep of the week-so-far high or low, only in 'internal' weeks. Only 4 of 125 NFP weeks met the declared internal test and 3 of those produced a trade, so n=3 < 30 and the harness verdict is UNTESTABLE. The trade itself is fully operationalised.
Plain 'never trade Monday' (18:00-NY session date) on the 15m CISD book. Tue-Fri vs Monday: -0.010R, powered NULL (MDE 0.045).
AM Trades form: Monday blocked, and Tuesday allowed only if Monday traded through the prior week's high or low. Result: powered NULL (MDE 0.037).

Pooled auto rungs: 1h CISD with 1D, 15m with 4H (forex grid), 5m with 1H. Gated = the last completed auto-paired HTF bar is a candle 2 in the event's direction. Result +0.008R, powered NULL (MDE 0.023).

1-minute step, which is the chart the worked example used. Setup: a 1h FVG tap is the POI, then an M1 close through the intermediate swing, entry at the midpoint of the M1 FVG, stop at the move extreme, target the nearest untaken 1h swing, 8h hold. Result: +0.017R vs matched random entry, CI [-0.086, +0.110], MDE 0.14, so not powered. Win rate 27%.
The 15-second execution step cannot be tested because the certified data is M1 only. There are no sub-minute bars to find a 15s FVG or swing stop, or to resolve a trade on.

Setup: a small-wick 1h bar closes beyond the prior bar's extreme inside a forming 4H candle (forex grid). Enter at the 50% retrace, stop at the expansion bar's extreme, exit at the 4H close. Result: +0.030R vs control, CI [-0.001, +0.060]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.044). The 'invert inside the wick' trigger is undefined in the source and was not modelled.

Gaps at the 18:00 NY reopen (including the Sunday reopen) that do not cross a prior D/W/M extreme fill back to the previous close within 60 M1 bars 67.5% of the time. The null is 63.0%: same signed distance, time of day held within 30 minutes. Diff +4.6pp, CI [+2.3, +6.7]pp, both halves agree (+5.2 / +4.1). This is only a campaign candidate. Caveat: most gold reopen gaps are tiny (median about 2% of the daily range). The fill may partly be the reopen quote/spread snapping back, not a tradeable fade, and this was not checked on a trade book.

Exception branch: gaps that cross a prior D/W/M extreme should fill LESS often than the null (claim '-'). They filled 35.5% vs a null of 26.2% (+9.3pp), which points against the claim, but the CI contains 0. Only n=110, so underpowered.

4H, the higher-timeframe case. The budget says take only the first 2 same-TF FVG taps after the curve low. Book: 2R, 40h hold. Taps 1-2 (n=467) vs taps 3+ (n=1820): +0.23R, CI [+0.087, +0.371]. The CI clears 0 in the claimed direction, but MDE is 0.20 > 0.10, so UNDERPOWERED. A candidate worth more data.
1H, the lower-timeframe case (budget of 1 tap). The first tap vs later taps: -0.087R, CI [-0.188, +0.010], leaning against the claim. MDE 0.14, so UNDERPOWERED.

1h MMXM. Blocks are the up-close candles between the range top and the curve low, entered on the retrace, stop at the block low, target the range top, 10h hold. Blocks with a nested same-direction FVG (n=8229) vs bare blocks (n=9534): -0.09R, CI [-0.31, +0.08]. The far range-top targets make R very noisy (MDE 0.28), so UNDERPOWERED.

15m MMXM state machine (H0, MSS, leg-1 FVG tap, ITH, BOS, leg-2 FVG tap). Leg-2 entries with the stop at the ITH (n=2722) vs leg-1 entries with the stop at H0 (n=8210), both 2R and a 150-minute hold: +0.009R, CI [-0.028, +0.047]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.054).

5m swing-level breaks. Entering on the first M1 close through the level (n=102k) vs waiting for the 5m close (n=98k), same 5m swing stop, 2R, 50-minute hold: +0.006R, CI [-0.004, +0.016]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.014). The early cut when the 5m fails to confirm was not modelled, because that exit depends on information after entry.

Limit entry at the mean threshold (50% of the whole series' bodies) of the 1h CISD order block, filled within 10 bars. Stop stays at the protected swing, 2R target, 10h hold. Compared with matched random entries: +0.013R [-0.027, +0.057]. Powered null (MDE 0.060).

Respect test: the first 1h retest into the block's body zone, split by whether the retest bar held the mean threshold (82% did). Held vs violated: +0.001R [-0.107, +0.111]. Underpowered, because the complement has only 947 trades (MDE 0.156).

Baseline is the rung-3 book (1h CISD, 2R, 10h). Gate is rung 2: an opposing FVG closed fully through between the extreme and the CISD, which fired on 26.5% of events. With vs without the inversion: -0.008R [-0.063, +0.046]. Powered null.

Candidate only, pending Holm/BH. Baseline is the 1h CISD book; gate is the POI search order from method_spec §4.1 (FVG, then swing, then CISD level; both tagged when both exist). The CISD-level fallback's look-forward is capped at the confirm bar. Pass rate 80.4%. Gated vs complement: +0.095R [+0.032, +0.161]; halves +0.060 / +0.124, block B1 negative. It works mostly by removing the complement, which runs -0.065R against its own control.

Same 1h CISD baseline. Gate is the loose closed list: any FVG tagged or any prior swing taken in the range, with no fallback and no both-required clause. Pass rate 64.4%. Gated vs complement: -0.048R [-0.106, +0.004]. Powered null that leans against the claim.

Target fixed first at the untaken prior-day high/low. The 15m CISD is traded when its R >= 2. Otherwise the book takes the earliest 5m or 1m CISD that gives R >= 2 to the same target, inside 150 minutes and before the target or the 15m stop is touched. Trades by timeframe: 15m 17,129; 1m 4,824; 5m 334. Against matched random entries: -0.028R [-0.052, -0.003].

C3 traded off the single C2 CISD alone: a 4h forex-grid C2 with a same-direction 15m CISD inside it, entered at the C2 close with the stop at the C2 extreme, 2R, held to the C3 close. Against matched random entries: +0.014R [-0.015, +0.044]. Powered null (MDE 0.042).

T-spot read as the C2 equilibrium (4h C2 with a 15m CISD). The rate at which C3 trades beyond the equilibrium is 63.4%, against 62.7% for a matched null (same distance and bars). Diff +0.006 [-0.010, +0.023]. Powered null.

T-spot read as the overlap of 0.5 of the C2 wick and 0.5 of the CISD series bodies, using the band's deeper edge. C3 trades beyond it 44.2% of the time, against 45.3% for the matched null. Diff -0.011 [-0.027, +0.005]. Powered null.

Baseline is the minimal-confirmation 4h C2 plus 15m CISD book. Gate is a proxy for 'strong structure', declared before the run: C1 is a clean small-wick expansion (opposing run / body <= 1.0) and C2 closes through the open of the HTF opposing series. It fired on 8.2% of events. Result: -0.020R [-0.101, +0.060]. Underpowered (gated n=389, MDE 0.115). Bias strength is discretionary in the corpus, and the medium and weak arms (continuation entry, SMT) were not tested.

Baseline is the 1h CISD book targeting the untaken prior-day high/low, 10h hold. Gate: entry sits in the swing-side half of the swing-to-target distance, which fired on 66.9% of events. Gated vs complement: +0.018R [-0.041, +0.076]. Powered null (MDE 0.084).

Gate test on the phase-3 15m CISD book. The gated arm meets at least 2 of the 3 criteria: PDH/PDL not yet taken, under half of the 5-day mean range used, entry within 0.25 of that range from the 18:00 open. Result +0.021R [-0.007, +0.046] against the 12,911 trades scoring 0 or 1. Powered, so NULL.

Daily candle governs. Gate on the 15m CISD book: entry at or below the daily open plus 0.25 of the typical range (mirrored for shorts), and the day's range not yet at the 5-day typical range. Result +0.024R [-0.003, +0.050]. Powered, so NULL.
4H candle governs (forex grid). Same gate as reading a, with the 4H candle's open and the mean range of the last 30 4H candles. Result +0.000R [-0.025, +0.025]. Powered, so NULL.

Trade test of pre-09:30 NY entries (07:00-09:30): 15m CISD with a protected-swing stop, the last closed 1D, 4H and 1H candles all in the trade direction, target PDH/PDL at least 2R away, exit by 16:00. Control held to the same NY hours (+/-30 min). Result -0.19R [-0.46, +0.09] on 181 trades, MDE 0.39. UNDERPOWERED.
Same setup, decided 07:00-12:00 NY. Gate compares pre-open entries (before 09:30) with post-open entries (09:30-12:00). Result -0.35R [-0.88, +0.14], 181 pre-open against 69 post-open. UNDERPOWERED.

Rate test on 15m FVGs at the first return to the near edge. A hit is price getting back to the leg extreme before a 15m close beyond the far edge, within 16 bars. The null uses the same distances and window from random times within +/-30 days. Hit rate 39.8% against 38.8% null, +0.96pp [+0.40, +1.53], halves agree (+1.01 / +0.92). EDGE, but only a candidate for Holm/BH, and the effect is small.

Trade test: a 1H CISD whose protected swing sits in the half of the previous day's range matching its direction (lows in [PDL, EQ] for longs, highs in [EQ, PDH] for shorts). Stop at that swing, target the far side (PDH/PDL) if not yet taken, 10h hold. Result -0.019R [-0.069, +0.033]. Powered, so NULL.

Later version, where the stop raid is a hard gate. 5m setup: raid of a swing low or high, then a structure break with displacement (threshold_fits 4 bars, r=1.5, d=0.65), then an unmitigated FVG in the discount or premium half of the move. Entry on the M1 return within 2h, stop at the gap's creating candle, 2R, 50min hold. Result -0.022R [-0.12, +0.07], MDE 0.138. UNDERPOWERED.

Earlier version, where the raid can be replaced by the move's origin trading into a completed 1H FVG from the prior 5 days. Otherwise the same as reading a. Result -0.005R [-0.088, +0.077], MDE 0.118. UNDERPOWERED.

Run on M1, because 15-second data does not exist here. A 30-bar up move (1.5x the prior range) stalls at a swing high, then the counter move closes below the leg's internal swing low and leaves an FVG. Entry on the return to the gap's near edge, stop at the high above the gap, target the 0.62 retracement of the move, 30min hold. Longs mirrored. Result +0.049R [-0.036, +0.165], MDE 0.144. UNDERPOWERED.

Gate test on second-and-later taps of 1h CISD order blocks (bar-close reaction entry, stop at the protected swing, 2R, 10h). Gate = the drawn objective (nearest unswept opposite 2/2 swing) is still untaken. Untaken taps (n=1765) vs taken taps: -0.022R [-0.100, +0.054]. MDE is 0.110 against the 0.10 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED.

Order-type mechanics with no claim to test: a limit entry with an OCO stop and target. The harness already resolves every trade as an OCO bracket, so there is nothing to compare it against. Stop-leg slippage needs fill or tick data, and no rule says where the limit goes.

Rate test: the day's first 15m CISD between 02:00 and 12:00 NY. Claim tested: its protected swing is the daily wick and is not traded through before the 17:00 NY halt. It held 24.4% of the time vs 25.5% for a null at matched distance, time of day and bar count: -0.011 [-0.029, +0.008]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.026).

Trade test. Setup: with the previous-candle daily bias, a counter-bias 5m opposing run from the 00:00, 08:30 or 09:30 NY open, then a CISD close back through it. Enter on that close, stop at the run's extreme, 2R, exit at 16:00 NY (hold measured in bars, clustered by date). Result -0.017R [-0.077, +0.041]: powered NULL (MDE 0.085).

Gate test of the Judas-swing price anchor on reading a's 08:30/09:30 trades. Gate = the run's extreme lies beyond both the midnight open and the 08:30 open. Gated n=958 vs 710: +0.048R [-0.092, +0.185]. MDE 0.198, so UNDERPOWERED.

Gate test on first returns to the opening price of 1h CISD order blocks (limit-touch entry, protected-swing stop, 2R, 10h). Gate = high-probability block candle, meaning opposing_run/body <= 1.0 (threshold_fits grade A). High-probability blocks (n=3788) vs low-probability (1790): +0.080R [+0.0003, +0.154]. The CI clears 0 in the claimed direction, but MDE is 0.110 against the 0.10 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED. Worth watching as a borderline positive.

Rate test, because the concept gives no stop. Event: the first 15m wick outside the Asia range (20:00-00:00 NY) that closes back inside with no earlier displacement close. Outcome: the Asia EQ is reached by 12:00 NY: 76.3% vs a matched null of 76.3%. Powered NULL. The Seek & Destroy day classification is discretionary and was not applied.

Trade test. 15m setup: sweep, then a close through structure, then an FVG, then a tap of the FVG. Trigger: a 5m Strat break of the previous 5m candle's extreme; stop at the trigger candles' extreme, 2R, 50 min. Result -0.005R [-0.053, +0.046]: powered NULL (MDE 0.071).

Trade test of the TTrades reading. Setup: a 15m sweep of a short-term swing at a 1h POI (PDL/PDH or an active 1h FVG), then within 4 bars a close back inside plus a same-direction 15m FVG. Entry: limit at the FVG CE; stop at the run low; 2R; 150 min. Result +0.081R [+0.030, +0.132], p=0.002; halves +0.128 and +0.042; ties are clean. EDGE is only a candidate before Holm/BH. Caveat: this is a limit-touch entry, entered on average 0.24R below the previous M1 open, while the random control does not share that dip conditioning. Checked the first 3-5 minutes: drift is only about +0.02R, so M1 bounce does not obviously explain the effect.

Trade test of the guest reading (Finessee_Fx): no structure break is used. Bias = the latest respected 1h CISD block, held until a 1h close violates it. Entry: first touch of the near edge of a 15m FVG in the bias direction; stop at the anchor's protected swing; 2R; 10h; clustered by anchor. Result +0.014R [-0.009, +0.038]: powered NULL. Pre-verdict fix (no test had run yet): holding the original block kept one 2016 bullish anchor for the whole decade and failed the lookahead probe, so the anchor now rolls to the latest same-direction block.

Tested whether a fresh 15m fractal-2/2 swing pool gets traded through within 360 M1 bars more often than a same-distance level at a matched random time: 69.8% vs 69.5%, a powered NULL. The first run's write was refused on params_source keys and the deterministic test was re-run once, with identical numbers; this is noted in the result.

Tested sweep-and-reject of untaken 15m pools, trading toward the nearest opposite pool with the stop at the sweep bar's extreme (6h hold, trading time, ToD-matched control). Diff +0.115R but MDE 0.28R: the stop is tight and the target far, so R is heavy-tailed. UNDERPOWERED.

Later canon: at the 18:00 NY open the draw is PDH or PDL, picked by the trend in prior-day extremes, with target = the draw and stop = the opposite level for one session. Diff +0.037R. MDE is 0.112 and the effective n of 1107 is below the power floor, so UNDERPOWERED. ctrl_overlap is 38%.

Follow the displacement: yesterday's close vs its open picks PDH or PDL, same bracket as reading a. Diff -0.016R and the CI contains 0. The ToD-matched controls are 49% the concept's own trades (daily 18:00 entries on almost every day), so the harness turned the NULL into UNDERPOWERED.

Swing-level sense: a symmetric bracket toward each confirmed 15m swing, gated on a failure swing (lower high / higher low = low resistance) vs a swing that swept the previous one (high resistance). Control-adjusted diff +0.0065R, a powered NULL (MDE 0.025).

Daily-band sense: the first break of PDH or PDL (stop at the day's running extreme, 2R), gated on at least 2 stacked unswept prior daily highs or lows in the path. Diff +0.013R; the gated arm has n=681 and MDE 0.115, so UNDERPOWERED. The corpus's circular 'market-conditions' sense was not tested.

Tested the premise that a high-resistance extreme (15m pool swept, closing back inside twice) is harder to reach, measured from the next opposite swing: reached 55.6% vs a same-distance null of 56.1% within 360 bars. Powered NULL; the extreme is not harder to reach than its distance implies.

15m bare-CISD book (2R, 150 min), gated on the reversal extreme running an untaken 1H fractal swing from the last 7 days, vs reversals that ran nothing. Gated n=2067 vs 30676, diff -0.024R, powered NULL. Before any test ran, the relevant pool was switched from PDH/PDL to 1H swings because PDH/PDL fired on only 1.2% of events; the switch is noted in the script docstring.

On low-expectation days (running range at least 75% of the 5-day ADR), a 15m extreme that swept 2 or more pools was reached before day end at 39.0% vs a null of 39.1%, a powered NULL. It was re-run once: run 1 had an EDGE (-0.021, CI [-0.039, -0.004]) caused by a null with no time-of-day match. Decisions cluster 10:00-17:00 NY, and those null windows fell in more active hours (trap 9). Run 2 matches the NY clock within +/-30 min. Both runs are ledgered and the result notes explain this.

Reversal SMT (XAU/EUR or XAU/GBP failed to take its C1 extreme on the C2 hour) used as a gate on the 1h small-wick C2 reversal book (2R, 10 bars): the SMT arm (44% of 7,520) was no better than the complement, powered NULL
Continuation SMT (exactly one of gold / gold-euro / gold-pound retook its C2 extreme during C3) used as a gate on the 1h sequential-C3 continuation book: +0.045R with the CI spanning 0, powered NULL
Head-to-head on 1h C2s where the correlate choices disagree (7,387): reversal SMT vs gold-euro/gold-pound (the instruments he names) against silver-only SMT. No difference, powered NULL (MDE 0.098)

15m first sweep of a 2/2 swing (wick through, close back) in the direction of 4H previous-candle-engine order flow; stop at the sweep bar, target the engineered-from swing. Diff vs control -0.058R, CI spans 0; UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.132, effective n 2,348)

Variant reading: a 15m sweep of a short-term swing followed within 4 bars by a same-direction FVG, entered at the FVG close, stop at the sweep extreme, target the opposite swing. Diff -0.022R, powered NULL
1h grab (the first bar through a 2/2 swing closes back inside), traded toward the opposite confirmed swing with the stop at the grab extreme. Diff +0.011R, CI spans 0; UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.114 > 0.10)

On 32,544 15m first sweeps of 2/2 swings, all traded as reversals at the close of bar j+2: the V-shape gate (close back through, distance/pre-range >= 0.65, range/pre-range >= 1.5 over 3 bars, 12.4% firing) did WORSE than lethargic sweeps by -0.057R; the CI excludes 0 against the claim, and the tie rule does not change the label
On inside-so-far days, first touch of the prior-day EQ: the bias-side PD extreme (the side the day opened on) was reached first 37.3% of the time vs a 36.1% geometry-matched null; powered NULL

TradingView pane and sync configuration with no market claim of its own. Its one substantive rule (same-candle SMT comparison) is the definition already used in this batch's SMT tests, and its measurable needs a record of visually spotted SMTs that does not exist

AM Trades reading. Setup: a Mon-Wed consolidation (no daily close beyond the prior day's range), then Thursday sweeps one side of the Mon-Wed external range, closes back inside and prints a 1h CISD. Trade on Friday: stop at Thursday's extreme, target the far side of the range. Only 23 setups in 10.5 years, below the harness's n>=30 floor, so the harness labels it UNTESTABLE for sample size, not because the rule can't be operationalised.

McJflkKuvrI variant. Thursday must take out both Monday's and Wednesday's extreme and close back beyond both; the 1h CISD and Friday trade are the same as reading a. Only 16 setups, below the n>=30 floor, so the harness labels it UNTESTABLE for sample size.

An attitude about not knowing, with no decision rule. The concept only says the weekly profile is not assigned before the week trades. It names no pre-week classifier to score: the 'Monday-morning guess' is never specified and the set of profiles is not listed. Its working parts (skip Monday; confirm with an hourly CISD) are separate concepts: no-monday-rule and hourly-cisd-manipulation-confirmation.

Trigger: the first 15m close beyond the -2.5 deviation of the previous 4H candle's manipulation leg (forex grid). The -4 deviation was then touched within 240 M1 bars 62.6% of the time vs 59.8% for a random-moment null at the same distance. The harness labels this EDGE, but it is almost certainly an artefact of the null design. A diagnostic at the SAME moments, with a target at the same distance in the OPPOSITE direction, is touched 62.5% of the time. So the excess reflects higher volatility after a strong close, not continuation toward -4. This is recorded in the result's notes, and it should not count as an edge.

Same rule with the 4H candle's own close beyond -2.5 as the trigger. The -4 deviation was reached within the next 240 bars 56.6% of the time vs 58.0% for the null. The point estimate is negative and the test is underpowered (MDE 0.070 vs 0.05).

Framework one: the 4H candle opens between the 1.0 and 1.5 deviation, and the claim is continuation to -2. Hit 66.7% vs 68.5% for a same-moment mirror level at the same distance in the opposite direction; that null was fixed before the run. The point estimate is slightly negative and the test is underpowered (MDE 0.056).

Framework two: the candle opens between the 2.0 and 2.5 deviation, and the claim is a retracement to the previous candle's 50% level. Hit 61.7% vs 64.6% for the same-moment mirror level. The point estimate is negative and the test is underpowered (MDE 0.078).

At Tuesday's close, trade against the week-to-date move away from the Monday 00:00 NY weekly open (long if Tuesday closed below it). Stop at the Mon+Tue extreme, no target, exit at Friday's close (69h, bars basis). avg R -0.078, diff vs matched control +0.039 with a wide CI. Underpowered (MDE 0.34), because the variance of R is high with no target. The weekly-bias and no-news preconditions could not be applied.

Gate 'buy at/below the weekly open (Monday 00:00 NY), sell at/above it' tested on the phase-3 locked 1h CISD baseline (7,513 events after the weekly open; 2,770 gated). Gated minus complement is +0.005R, CI [-0.054, +0.066]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.086): entry location relative to the weekly open adds nothing.

The data has no volume, so the balance area is a time-at-price (TPO) stand-in: the previous day's 70% value area and point of control (POC). Event: the first M1 close back inside after closing outside. The POC was touched before the day ended 65.0% of the time vs 63.6% for a same-moment mirror level at the same distance in the opposite direction. Powered NULL (MDE 0.041). Only the first target (the POC) is tested.

The daily next-day decision table was traded on day D+1: continuation (1,132 days) or reversal (868). Entry at the D+1 open, stop at D's extreme, 2R target, one session held in trading time. Result: -0.010R against a matched control, a powered null (MDE 0.064). The first run was not written because the tested frame lacked its state column; it was re-run once with the same book and gave identical numbers (recorded in the notes).
After a reversal day (a 2-2 reversal), day D+1 reached D-1's opposite extreme 30.0% of the time, against 30.7% for a null with the same distance and bar count. Powered null (MDE 0.048).

Gate on the bare 15m CISD book: take only trades in the direction of the developing daily candle (sign of the last close minus the 18:00 open). Gated trades beat the complement by +0.031R after control adjustment. Both halves agree (+0.029/+0.034). This is an EDGE candidate only: p=0.029 is marginal and is unlikely to survive Holm correction across the campaign.

Same 15m CISD baseline. The gate adds a supported-direction test: the developing daily candle's opposing run must be at most 1.0x its body. Result: +0.027R, halves +0.012/+0.041. This is a borderline EDGE candidate (the CI's low end is +0.0002, p=0.049). It shares its baseline with reading a, so it is not independent evidence.
Gate on the 5m CISD entry book: the entry direction agrees with the daily bias from the previous-candle engine on the last completed day. Result: +0.005R, a powered null (MDE 0.025).

Full Daily -> 1H -> 5m ladder: the daily bias agrees with the entry and the 5m setup's swept extreme took out the previous completed 1H candle's low or high (the hourly POI). Result: +0.015R, a powered null (MDE 0.031).

Book of 1H C2 closures traded as C3: stop at C2's extreme, 2R, two 1H candles held. The gate requires a 5m CISD inside C2 (closure plus CISD, against closure alone). Result: -0.031R, a powered null leaning against the claim. ctrl_overlap was 0.195, just under the 0.20 cap.
The same test on the 4H (forex grid) -> 15m pair. Result: -0.032R, MDE 0.102, just over the 0.10 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED.

Every directional 4H candle, traded as a continuation into the next 4H candle: stop at the candle's opposite extreme, time exit only. The gate is a small wick (opposing run / body <= 1.0). Result: +0.016R, a powered null (MDE 0.070).
Same 4H continuation book with the range form of the small-wick gate (opposing run / range <= 0.30). Result: +0.025R, a powered null (MDE 0.061).
Gate on the bare 5m CISD book: the last completed 1H candle is a C2 or C3 (reading A) closure in the entry's direction (the 1H -> 5m pair). Result: -0.010R, a powered null (MDE 0.025).
Same test on the 4H (forex grid) -> 15m pair. Result: -0.006R, a powered null (MDE 0.043).

Seek & Destroy as a stand-aside day, applied to 15m CISD trades in NY a.m. (08:30-12:00). A day is S&D when London took both Asia extremes. Non-S&D days gave +0.023R. Only about 3% of days are S&D (556 trades in that arm), so the MDE is 0.125: UNDERPOWERED.

London counter-run then New York continuation (the London Reversal and NY Reversal profiles pooled). The gate requires a daily bias, London running counter to it beyond the Asia extreme, no S&D, and a NY entry in the bias direction. Result: +0.003R, MDE 0.113, UNDERPOWERED.

Daily candle 4 trade. Needs a 3-candle swing, with C3 closing beyond C2's extreme and closing strong (close position >= 0.85). Entry at the C4 open, stop at 0.5 of C3's range, 2R, one day held. Only 172 trades in the certified span; -0.107R, UNDERPOWERED.
The same C4 trade on 4H forex-grid candles. Result: -0.040R, MDE 0.120, UNDERPOWERED.

Book of 4H C2 closures traded as C3. The gate is an ideal C2: the same bar closes beyond the open of the opposing-candle series into its extreme. 15.6% of C2s qualify. Result: -0.070R, leaning against the claim, MDE 0.116, UNDERPOWERED.
The same ideal-formation gate on daily C2 closures. Only 141 are ideal; -0.029R, UNDERPOWERED.

Tested the stand-aside rule as a gate with claim '-'. Baseline: 15m bare CISD trades in NY 08:30-12:00. Gate: S&D day, meaning London takes both Asia extremes and closes back inside the Asia range (about 5% of days). Result: diff -0.004R, MDE 0.19, effective n 128.

Outside-in deviation trade on S&D days: a 15m bar in NY AM takes London's high or low and closes back inside. Target is London EQ, stop is the deviation extreme, hold 150 min. Too few trades to decide.

Earlier 'Next Day Model' reading. The previous day reacted off an unfilled daily FVG. The trade is the next session only, never Monday, NY 08:30-12:00, first 15m CISD away from the level, 2R, 150 min. Underpowered (MDE 0.24).

Canonical reading: PDH/PDL raid, 15m CISD as the MSS substitute, hourly silver SMT proxy, midnight-open side filter. Target is the nearest unmitigated 1h FVG edge, stop at the raid extreme. Result: diff -0.059R, MDE 0.18, so not powered.

15m model: sweep of the prior 20-bar range, CISD back inside, limit-style entry on a retest of the CISD level within 150 min, premium/discount filter. Stop at the manipulation extreme, target the -2 SD projection (2R). Powered null (MDE 0.057).

Monday or Tuesday daily C2 closure that is the week's extreme, with an hourly CISD inside the day. Enter at the C3 open, stop at the extreme, 2R, hold to Friday 17:00 NY in trading minutes. MDE 0.24, effective n 175.

15m aggressive out-and-back of the prior 20-bar range, with 'aggressive' set by the threshold_fits displacement magnitude (N=4, r=1.5, d=0.65). Trade toward the opposite range extreme, stop at the excursion, 150 min. Null, barely powered (MDE 0.092).

Shorts reading: Monday and Tuesday both continuation closures, then a Wednesday C2 that is not the week extreme, with an hourly CISD. Only 4 events in 10.5 years, below n=30, so the harness rules it UNTESTABLE. It is too rare to decide, not unmeasurable.
Series reading: Monday continuation closure, then the first Tue-Thu C2 in that direction that is not the week extreme, with an hourly CISD. Trade the next day to Friday's close, 2R. Only 43 trades.

Monday and Tuesday close against the setup, then Wednesday is a C2 week extreme with an hourly CISD. Enter at the Thursday open, stop at Wednesday's extreme, 2R, hold to Friday close. Only 71 trades, MDE 0.63.

Friday-reversal reading. Week extreme on Mon/Tue, Wed and Thu expansion, previous week's extreme hit by Thursday. Friday sweeps Thursday's extreme and a 1h CISD confirms, target a 25% weekly-range retracement. 26 events, 17 after target-behind-entry drops, below n=30, so UNTESTABLE. The +0.55R on n=17 means nothing.

Thursday-reversal reading: Thursday is a counter daily C2 with an hourly CISD, short at the Friday open with a 25% retracement target. 72 events, but 54 had already reached the target by Thursday's close, leaving 18 trades. Below n=30, so UNTESTABLE.

A 4H forex-grid C2 plus a 1H CISD inside it, at the day's extreme so far: that extreme held to the end of the NY day 53.7% of the time, against 50.4% for a null matched on distance, M1 bars and NY time of day. Diff +3.4pp. Halves H1 +5.6 and H2 +1.6. This is a candidate only and needs the Holm/BH pass.

The nearer previous-month extreme was reached before the far one 42.0% of the time, against 49.4% for a null with the same two distances and horizon. That is the opposite of the claim. Clustered by month, effective n=114. Re-run once after a bug in my null (details in the note).

Bias from a 1H C2/C3 closure, then a 15m C2 that forms the next hour's wick, entered at the 15m close with a stop at the swing, 2R target, 60-minute hold. +0.010R against the matched control, powered NULL (MDE 0.036).

1H displacement (threshold_fits N=4, r=1.5, d=0.65) plus an FVG in the window, with the draw set at the nearest untaken swing beyond it. The draw was reached the same NY day 42.5% of the time vs a 42.4% matched null. Powered NULL. Reading b, the London/Asia narrative, gives no rule and was not run.

15m sequence: sweep, structure break, then entry when the internal (inducement) low is run. Stop at the protected low, target the range high, 150-minute hold, no FVG required. -0.020R against the control, powered NULL.
Same sequence as reading a, but a same-direction FVG overlapping the inducement candle is required (his stated preference). -0.012R, powered NULL.
Silver (local OANDA XAG H1) prints a 1H C2 and gold does not. Gold's next hour is traded as C3 on a 5m retracement plus CISD, targeting gold's C2-hour extreme. -0.009R, powered NULL.

Raid of the 09:00 NY hour's high or low between 10 and 11, a 1m CISD entry, stop at the sweep extreme, target the other side of the 09:00 candle, 120-minute hold, control matched on time of day. -0.011R, MDE 0.131 > 0.10, so UNDERPOWERED.

Daily previous-candle bias; after 08:30 NY, a sweep of the 00:00-08:30 range extreme on the bias side (so below the midnight open for longs); 5m CISD entry, stop at the swept extreme, target the far side of that range, exit 16:00. +0.048R, MDE 0.137, UNDERPOWERED.

Weekly C2 bias, then a daily C2 plus a 1H CISD in that direction, entered at the daily close with a stop at the daily extreme, target the weekly draw (only if at least 2R away), exit at the week close. Only 41 trades in 10.5 years, so UNDERPOWERED. Re-run once with hold_basis='bars' under trap 7, because the clock run showed a 33% exposure mismatch.

Rate test. During daily consolidation (5-day mean range < 0.8x the prior 20 days, bodies < 0.5x range), an alert sits above the top of the nearest open bearish daily FVG above price. When it fires, the nearest unbroken daily swing high was hit within 5 sessions 33.3% of the time vs 39.4% for the matched null. n=33, MDE 0.25: far too few events to decide.

Gate test on the guest's own model: 1h leg of at least 1 ATR, M1 touch of the 50% retracement, stop at the leg origin, target at the leg extreme, 10h hold. Expansive regime (48-bar 1h efficiency ratio >= 0.20, gated n=3,051) vs range-bound (n=6,393): +0.046R [-0.020, +0.108]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.091). The trade-the-range branch has no threshold and was not tested.

Base book: 1h CISD with T1 = nearest unbroken 1h swing at least 0.25R away. At the first adverse 15m close through the latest 15m swing before T1 or the stop, holding the original stop/T1 bracket for the rest of the 10h hold vs a matched random control: -0.028R [-0.073, +0.021]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.067): the adverse shift carries no information, so not moving the stop costs nothing, and moving it would not have helped either.

Scored the post-T1 runner leg of 1h CISD trades that reached T1 before the stop: stop moved to break-even at entry, T2 = prior-day high/low beyond T1, 10h hold. Vs a matched random control: +0.032R [-0.071, +0.132]. MDE 0.145 misses the 0.10 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED. The 20% partial at T1 is booked the same way under any variant and is not scored.

Pure sizing and account-capital advice: start small, step up in micro-contract increments, halve size when panicking. Per-trade R does not change with contract count, the triggers ('earned', 'panic') are subjective, and the measurables need a trader's journal, not OHLC.

A prop-firm size ladder (a ~$2,000 cushion, then about 20 micros, then 1-5 ES). This is sizing arithmetic tied to a firm's drawdown rules and the trader's own confidence. There is no setup, R does not change with size, and testing it needs prop-account equity records.

An execution-quality claim (a stop order may not fill at its level). Testing it needs broker fill records or bid/ask ticks. The dataset is a mid-quote M1 OHLC series, and the harness always fills stops at the stop level or the gap open.

Compares limit fill rates between a futures feed and a spread-quoted forex feed on the same setups. We have one XAUUSD mid M1 series with no bid/ask spread and no futures counterpart, so neither fill rate can be computed.

Compares asset classes: gapping cash equities/ETFs vs continuous futures. Only near-continuous XAUUSD data is available, so gap incidence and profile agreement across instrument classes cannot be measured.
30m rung-0 CISD with the stop at 50% of the opposing-candle series and a 2R target vs a matched random control: +0.001R, a powered zero. Price does not respect the half level more than random.

Mechanical trail events inside open 15m CISD positions (stop moved to each new opposing candle's extreme, clustered by parent) vs a random stop at the same distance: -0.015R, NULL. The trailed levels do not hold better than random ones.

Gate on the 15m rung-0 CISD book: entries taken while the day's range so far is below ADR(20) beat entries after the ADR is covered by +0.039R (control-adjusted); both halves positive. EDGE candidate only (p=0.033, must survive Holm/BH).

Same gate using the expansion-day band (median range of the expansion days among the last 20, with opp_run/body<=1.0): +0.040R, both halves positive (H2 weaker, +0.022). Largely the same mask as reading a (87-88% kept in both). EDGE candidate only.

When a 15m CISD 2R position reaches +1R and then returns to entry, holding on with the original stop and target vs a matched random entry: +0.036R, NULL (powered, MDE 0.062). The return to entry predicts neither failure nor success, so break-even vs a structural stop is a wash. The pro-break-even reading is the mirror (-) of this same statistic and was not run separately.

15m CISD signals fired while a 1D CISD swing is open, split into against the swing (kept as a hedge) and same direction (skipped): +0.010R, NULL. The rule's selection costs nothing per trade, so the exposure reduction comes free. The exposure claim itself is arithmetic.

Pure sizing arithmetic (risk = drawdown/N). Rescaling R cannot change a book's control-adjusted expectancy, and surviving N losses holds by construction. It needs a strategy's loss-streak distribution and a firm's rules, not a claim about gold.
Prop-account sizing and economics (percent of drawdown tiers, drawdown-to-target ratio, fees). This is arithmetic plus firm terms, none of which is in XAUUSD OHLC, and no gold test can decide it.

4h rung-0 CISD book (~3.9 signals a week, near his cadence), first two signals of the week vs the 3rd and later: +0.031R, MDE 0.14 > 0.10, so UNDERPOWERED; the halves disagree. Day of week is confounded with the rule by construction. Descriptively, the 1D CISD fires 35 times a year vs his 6-8 swing setups.

Fixed-dollar risk with size solved from the stop is a sizing procedure. The harness already scores every book in constant-R terms, so there is no alternative arm, and contract/micro rounding is a futures spec absent from spot data.

15m CISD book, protected-swing stop where the extreme swept a prior intact 2/2 swing (20.6% of events) vs a fresh swing: -0.018R, a powered NULL, both halves slightly negative. Stops behind already-swept liquidity are not safer.

Gate on the 15m CISD book: 2R target inside the remaining expansion-day budget (running day low/high plus the expansion band) vs beyond it: +0.018R, a powered NULL (H1 +0.041, H2 -0.003). A target ceiling adds nothing beyond the 'range already covered' gate.

Corollary 'after a very large range day (>1.5x ADR20) expect a smaller range': the next day's range was below ADR only 43% of the time vs 56% on matched random days. NEGATIVE: volatility clusters, and big days are followed by big days.

Reading a: a daily FVG counts as inverted when a daily close goes beyond the whole gap. Entry was a kill-zone M1 touch of the level within 5 days, stop at the gap's far side, target the inversion day's extreme. Result -0.17R vs control, CI [-0.41, +0.06]. MDE 0.33 is far above the 0.10 threshold.

Reading b: inversion needs only a daily close beyond the gap's mean threshold. Same kill-zone retest book as reading a. Result -0.17R, CI [-0.42, +0.07]. The sign is negative in both halves but the test is underpowered (about 290 daily events).

Baseline: days that take one side of the previous day, traded in the breach direction at the daily close (1R, one day hold). Gate: the day closed its body through PDH/PDL. The body-close continuation did worse than the wick-only breach, -0.093R, CI [-0.177, -0.011]. That is against the claim, with both halves negative.

Daily FVGs: first retest within 10 bars, traded with the array (stop at its far side, 2R). Gate: the retest bar did not close beyond the mean threshold. The gate passes 91% of the time, so the complement is only 33 trades. Result -0.29R, CI [-0.87, +0.27].
Same book on 1H FVGs. Retests that held the mean threshold vs retests that closed beyond it: +0.012R, CI [-0.108, +0.137]. The halves disagree. MDE 0.176 because the complement is only 638 trades.

Daily inside bar, traded on the next day's first M1 break. Target the mother bar's extreme, stop the inside bar's far side, one-day hold on bars. Result +0.054R vs control, CI [-0.010, +0.120]. Powered (MDE 0.093), so NULL.

Weekly outside bar: last week's high or low taken on Monday or Tuesday, then a counter 1h CISD. Target the other side of last week, stop the week's extreme, hold to the week's close. Result -0.09R, CI [-0.33, +0.17]. Only 160 weeks, so underpowered. Re-run on hold_basis=bars per trap 7.

Gate on the 4h CISD rung-0 book (forex grid, 2R, 40h hold on bars): does the trade agree with the monthly candle's side of its open? With-continuity trades did worse, -0.078R, CI [-0.183, +0.029]. MDE 0.152, so underpowered.

Tested whether the block extreme gets taken later in the day when the Asia low/high coincides with the PDL/PDH (within 0.10 daily ATR) and the Asia range is choppy (at most 0.5 ATR). It was hit 70.9% of the time against a matched null of 72.4%. Powered NULL. Two bugs were fixed before the verdict: a day_end off-by-one gave n=0 and was re-run, and a decision stamp at a data gap was caught by the probe.
